entries.title: Independent Web Environment Center
entries.summary: Desktop combines an environment center with its existing local Runtime lifecycle. Web Center deploys independently; Runtime never requires Center or Desktop to start. Both hosts share Contracts/Core/Controller/UI. Web Center has one administrator, with no registration, users, roles, organizations or user ACL service.

entries.title: Single-administrator Web Center access
entries.summary: Center has one administrator and multiple devices. Center, Gateway and Runtime authorize independently: directory/open access never bypasses Runtime login or grants host management. Device revocation cancels all derived admissions while retaining unrelated devices and routes.

entries.title: Deploy and qualify standalone Web Center
entries.summary: Center binary/UI deploy independently of Runtime/Desktop. Qualification records source/artifacts, host/browser, real duration, cleanup and limits using isolated names/ports/state. Preserve existing Runtime; smoke checks certify neither eight-hour soak nor a different native browser.

entries.title: Flower startup and recovery presentation
entries.summary: Both carriers project one readiness owner and typed Stop/Retry, retaining drafts/navigation. Close failure needs restart; contradictory facts are nonretryable. Initial content admits workspace, then refresh/reconnect preserves mounted state without another availability controller.

entries.title: Flower persistent-index startup acceptance
entries.summary: Published Floret 7.52.0 on an isolated 710,344,704 B/219-thread database achieves full product construction/activation P95 9.429 s over 20 runs, with maximum GC-live heap 261.052 MiB upstream/295.018 MiB product. Targets≤10 s/350 MiB pass for this dataset; canonical validation still has substantial temporary allocation.

entries.title: Flower conversation switch performance qualification
entries.summary: Published Floret v7.87.3 owns windows, bounded item-text reads, View/Summary. Redeven owns [sidebar](../ui/flower-thread-sidebar.md), [bridge](../desktop/desktop-runtime-bridge.md) and bounded presentation. Local targets: short-detail P95 reduction ≥70%, warm synchronous P95 <8 ms, feedback before commit.

entries.title: Flower conversation selection and detail reads
entries.summary:
Flower acknowledges navigation before transcript work. One coordinator serves
navigation, command confirmation and reference preflight. ThreadCache owns
selection and detail; the loader owns bounded ephemeral demand.
Readiness controls reveal; elapsed time controls feedback only.

entries.title: Control-plane capacity qualification
entries.summary: Capacity acceptance runs10000 Runtime sessions through real Nginx/TLS/MySQL and canonical admission with production heartbeat/recovery. Combine client latency/recovery with independently measured server CPU/RSS/database/queues/challenges; client success alone is insufficient.

entries.title: Tessiven DSL versioning
entries.summary: Runtime owns contiguous v1→v1.0.0→v1.1.0 migration. New canvases use v1.1.0; edges change version only, retaining legacy layout. Reads preserve YAML/digest/revision; writes save current snapshots. Invalid/unknown/migration-failed state remains unchanged for explicit repair.

entries.title: Tessiven stable canvas presentation
entries.summary: Runtime projects DSL into frozen data-only presentation/v1 for bundled renderers. DSL releases require no display-format/client changes. Preserve YAML/digest/revision/write authority; unsupported source remains viewable/exportable without guessed topology, but integrity failure cannot export.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas contract
entries.summary: Runtime owns immutable Tessiven service canvases: each save creates a version containing complete v1.1.0 YAML. Desktop Welcome and local Env App render the same library. Validation/version conflict preserves the last saved document; clients hold no separate canonical library.

entries.title: Native Runtime bridge
entries.summary: native-bridge --state-root attaches only to existing Runtime via owner socket. Stdio uses redeven-native-runtime-h2/1 and native-runtime CONNECT. Missing/stopped/incompatible targets fail without install/start/address fallback/Desktop credentials; disconnect releases client only.

entries.title: Flower working files and deliverables
entries.summary: Flower keeps intermediates in Runtime state and finals at the user's destination. Redeven owns bytes, filesystem policy and UI; Floret owns canonical results and identities. Files, Fork and cleanup preserve this boundary without another artifact index, transcript, upstream API or domain migration.

entries.title: Flower browser source ownership
entries.summary: Runtime authorizes targets; source Host owns CDP/extension adapters. Discovery grants no input. Each page has one debugger/input order; opener ancestry stays private. Source loss retires affected bindings only; unknown effects never replay or create replacement authority.

entries.title: Flower browser Linux preparation
entries.summary: Runtime discovers installs/registers Native Messaging; Host Applications owns graphical lifecycle. Linux guide prepares persistent Chrome profiles without launch/target authority. Clients pass opaque IDs. Personal profiles remain; missing/unsafe/unsupported sources fail before launch.

entries.title: Database schema migration ownership
entries.summary: Each repository migrates its own opaque stores. Validate full SQLite/WAL before readiness; contiguous atomic edges preserve records. Future, drifted, wrong-kind or unsupported state remains untouched. Failure blocks only its service without upstream repair or database replacement.

entries.title: AI readiness and service generation lifecycle
entries.summary: One process-local Redeven controller owns AI construction/retry/publication/leases/drain/close; Floret owns durable facts. Non-AI surfaces stay usable. Requests bind one generation; failed readiness returns typed sanitized state without partial publication or Store repair.

entries.title: Runtime startup presentation
entries.summary: `redeven run` startup is modeled as a lifecycle event stream. Human terminal output and public machine events are renderers over the same state snapshot, while a separate private Desktop report carries machine-only attach data and stable failure codes needed to open or recover the local Env App safely.

entries.title: Observation and target action events
entries.summary: Target actions are ordinary Flower tool observations. The workspace stream remains the only lifecycle and replay channel; screenshot descriptors are canonical keyframes, while short-lived live frames are target-scoped media and may be dropped without changing thread state.

entries.title: Local UI surface
entries.summary: Local UI supports independent concurrent Desktop/browser sessions. Public HTTP(S)/WS(S) shares a port; Desktop private uses numeric loopback protocol. Versioned SQLite owns one-shot authorization/spend; network policy owns exposure/password/certificates/migrations.

entries.title: Env App session event transport
entries.summary: One Floe HTTP proxy runtime serves each Env App session and all built-in/plugin logical event streams. Features cannot consume parallel native HTTP/1.1 slots, retarget upstream identity or create another transport. Session replacement cancels observations; stopping observation never cancels business work.

entries.title: Activity navigation restoration
entries.summary: One Redeven Activity record selects the saved target before mounting and commits navigation/recency immediately. Floe owns geometry only. Invalid targets use available built-ins or Terminal; transient inventory failure retains the target, and late restoration never overrides a newer user selection.

entries.title: Env App resource snapshots
entries.summary: Floe owns disposable cache restoration/coalescing/fencing/persistence/eviction; Redeven verifies identity/projection. Resource lists retain successful data while refresh animates only its icon. Cache grants nothing; denial clears, connectivity failure retains facts with Retry.

entries.title: Redeven loading and layout continuity
entries.summary: One registry declares initial/reload presentation for built-in Activity/Workbench surfaces. Load modules locally while retaining successful content. Services own readiness; authentication/authority changes override retention. Loading states never grant permission or replace recovery.

entries.title: Env App document reload presentation
entries.summary: Floe owns the anonymous reload geometry placeholder; Redeven hands it to current Activity inventory. Never replace restored content with a blank or mismatched skeleton. Geometry grants no data/authority. Denial, navigation, errors or auth change end it, and unavailable storage cannot block startup.

entries.title: Web Services interface
entries.summary: Activity/Workbench share service list/drawer: identity, state, action, facts. Retain narrow/localized/large-text usability. Historical failure never replaces current state; failed checks preserve facts and authorized recovery. Resource cache grants no lifecycle or route authority.

entries.title: Web Service browser sessions
entries.summary: Web Services opens current-Environment loopback ports/deep links through authorized forwarding. Registry access_mode alone selects unified_proxy or HTTP-only Desktop loopback. Reject other targets, stale/mismatched/expired routes and invalid modes before opening; no heuristic fallback.

entries.title: Managed host application preparation
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps verifies/stages/activates Linux components; Redeven routes/progress/placement. No VM/container/package manager/admin password is needed. Runtime updates are independent; optional failure retains compatible installs. Activation requires graphical qualification.

entries.title: Human remote desktop sessions
entries.summary: Redeven owns authorization/sessions/placement/audit; Floe Native Apps owns OS capture/input/codecs/playback and Linux acquisition/service. Share signed-in desktop without private replacement or policy changes. Disconnect preserves work; unavailable media revokes input until fresh frame.

entries.title: Administrator-authorized remote desktop deployment over SSH
entries.summary: Desktop owns SSH authorization/UI lifetime, Floe Native Apps privileged preparation and Runtime service authorization/audit. Every connection ensures current policy and authenticates actual Runtime. Unknown state is preserved. Cancellation reports rollback; verified completion may win but cannot auto-open after cancel.

entries.title: Persistent remote desktop sharing approval
entries.summary: Redeven owns sharing preference/reset; Floe Native Apps owns OS consent/private recovery. Logged-in Runtime may reuse saved approval, which proves no admission and never reaches viewers/URLs/audits. This user Portal path is separate from SSH system-service deployment.

entries.title: Remote desktop connection launcher
entries.summary: One Host Applications/Workbench flow identifies host, readiness and primary action, continuing consent in place under session policy. Failure retains recovery; dismissing pending creation releases its session. Once opened, viewer lifetime is independent of the launcher.

entries.title: Flowersec transport for graphical windows
entries.summary: Flowersec owns encrypted multiplexed transport/backpressure; Redeven resources/authorization/routes. Graphical state, tickets, input, clipboard/audio/pixels/disconnect use native proxy; static acquisition stays authenticated browser traffic. No missing-authority or raw HTTP/WS bypass.

entries.title: Graphical window native transport qualification
entries.summary: Published graphical transport passes direct, encrypted tunnel, authority and Linux checks. Host lock blocks active macOS capture/Electron fullscreen; locked-host refusal does not qualify unlocked use. Functional results remain separate from performance qualification.

entries.title: Remote desktop viewer interaction
entries.summary: Published input/playback and session contracts own current-frame authority. Separate cursors permit immediate movement; embedded cursors hide local pointer. Recovery keeps controls usable; disconnect stops media/input with confirmed removal or Retry. Frozen pixels never imply connection.

entries.title: Remote desktop media and input scheduling
entries.summary: Published native packages own capture/encode/playback; session contract owns authority/generations. Bound media work and align cursors to painted pixels. Input admission proves no delivery; capture/input failures retire authority and late work cannot replace successors.

entries.title: Wayland cursor and scheduling optimization evidence
entries.summary: Native 0.22.12 qualifies separate cursor/scheduling semantics with synthetic PipeWire frames. Input replies cannot block capture/authority; damage must retain post-gap changes. Fresh GNOME consent fails HOST_CONSENT_TIMEOUT, so distribution tests establish no live-GNOME latency. October 5 user waiver covers udesk24 performance only.

entries.title: Wayland legacy MemFd capture compatibility
entries.summary: Readable authorized MemFd frames must work when older producers omit MAPPABLE. The repair validates size/aligned offset/pixel range before mapping; 19 native tests pass. The normal udesk24 product reproduces CAPTURE_LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED, but repaired real GNOME capture and complete release qualification remain unpassed.

entries.title: Wayland capture pool optimization evidence
entries.summary: Native 0.22.14 replaces full-frame copies with a bounded pool.36 native tests pass. Alternating udesk24 synthetic 1440p60/x264 improves encoded 46.86–48.06→59.90 FPS and capture 19.34–19.96→2.64–2.79 ms; paint ACK improves too. This is not live GNOME or physical-input certification.

entries.title: Current-desktop acceptance method
entries.summary: Qualify the desktop contract using published dependencies/GOWORK=off. Preserve failures and meet agreed-host thresholds before acceptance; integration, a picture, admitted input or synthetic fixture cannot substitute for real performance. The acceptance record owns measured results and remaining work.

entries.title: Current-desktop qualification results
entries.summary: Native 0.22.6 passes scoped Mac/X11 office, performance and ten-minute queue/input checks. Mac minima 57.582/57.657 FPS cover 1080p/1440p. udesk24 is functional-only with retained Wayland failures; 0.22.7 owns later reconnect tests. Integration proves neither full release acceptance nor hardware encoding/parity.

entries.title: Remote desktop latency and NVIDIA encoding
entries.summary: Native 0.22.29 physical-seat and 0.22.10 X11/NVIDIA lanes measure different paths. X11 candidate click P95 improves 84.8→71.7 ms(light),88.3→75.2 ms(scroll), with lower decode-to-draw. Results qualify named hardware/configurations only, not photons, universal GPUs, zero-copy or WAN behavior.

entries.title: Remote desktop drag latency
entries.summary: October 4 X11/Floe 0.81.6 over Desktop SSH/HTTP 2 observes lower drag latency on i7-14700KF/RTX4090D/1080p60. Four baseline P95s84.06–86.51 ms and three candidate 69.13–74.06 ms retain all runs. Correlated frames cannot establish physical-photon latency or NoMachine parity.

entries.title: Physical desktop responsiveness and local input
entries.summary: Native v0.22.33 wakes capture; Floe owns pointer/text. Physical locks and generation/mode changes revoke input. Independently verify document, DRM and encoded output. udesk26 passes; Orange AFBC has separate follow-up. Native evidence is not full Viewer/performance acceptance.

entries.title: Orange AFBC capture qualification
entries.summary: Native 0.22.34 decodes Orange 1920×1080 Wayland legacy AFBC through EGL. Real pixels/lock/unlock and udesk26 regression pass; unsupported layouts reject. Input still requires privileged service/fresh paint. Native checks do not certify product update, browser/network latency or physical photons.

entries.title: Physical-device remote desktop Viewer qualification
entries.summary: Native 0.22.34 on udesk26 qualifies real Viewer picture/input, assisted Unicode, physical unlock, switching, fullscreen/disconnect and ten socket-loss recoveries. Median recovery 2015.7 ms/P95 2230.2 ms excludes photons. Real IME, matched cursor, command RTT, complete Orange acceptance and parity remain unqualified.

entries.title: Orange remote desktop Viewer follow-up
entries.summary: Orange 0.22.37 passes thirteen release jobs and Viewer Unicode/lock/unlock/input/media checks. Mac Pinyin is deferred; host Pinyin unvalidated. Improved paired latency/FPS does not erase missing idle responses/SSH recovery failures or later RustDesk tails/disconnects; measured LAN loss limits comparison.

entries.title: Physical desktop RustDesk comparison
entries.summary: Full RustDesk parity/historical repeatability remain unaccepted. Native v0.22.48 six-frame, three rounds: mean FPS 46.21 vs 32.54; pooled P95 310.60 vs 207.59 ms; >250ms gaps nine vs three. Round three reaches 53.04 FPS/150.20ms with no gaps, but cannot replace adverse round one. Preserve safeguards; C05/decision ledger own results and experiments.

entries.title: LAN desktop experiment decision ledger
entries.summary: LAN measurements show a deficit, not its cause or RustDesk parity. Published v0.22.48 reaches53.04FPS once without three-round stability. C01–C03 are rejected; C04 six-frame Linux is a throughput diagnostic. C05 retains paired outcomes, adverse trials and remaining limits.

entries.title: Published LAN C05 outcomes and unresolved boundaries
entries.summary: C05 retains all paired outcomes: six-frame delivery exceeds51FPS but not three-round stability/RustDesk parity. Lost source input invalidates latency; missing presentation with complete input is failure. Retry only documented fixture repair or discriminating hypotheses.

entries.title: Published six-frame LAN qualification C05
entries.summary: C05 owns qualification under the comparison contract. Optional six-frame delivery requires published native bytes and preserves legacy/macOS behavior. C04 proves diagnostic throughput, not recovery or RustDesk parity. Failed release gates/fixtures stop acceptance with retained evidence.

entries.title: Remote desktop platform reacceptance
entries.summary: October 17 task-owned reacceptance uses consumer 7230cf1ae40316efed23c6ff572d03656aded6cc, epoch 62, native Go 0.23.3/Swift 0.22.27/Electron 41.10.7. Actual pixels/input qualify named platform behaviors only; service startup alone proves neither Runtime authentication nor capture. Audio, latency, hotplug and first-time TCC remain excluded.

entries.title: Desktop reconnect qualification results
entries.summary: Native 0.22.7 reconnects Linux/macOS AudioWorklet sound and requires fresh paint for input. X11 two 100-sample rounds yield 66.5/67.6 ms input-paint P95. Mac lock/hotplug and Wayland mode recovery are separately scoped; udesk24 performance stays unpassed and functional-only.

entries.title: Wayland desktop qualification results
entries.summary: udesk24 GNOME 46/native 0.22.7 passes office/mode recovery but still fails 1080p/1440p scrolling at 27.458/23.458 FPS after authorized graphics provisioning. User designated functional-only on October 2. Preserve failures; X11 and synthetic fixtures cannot replace them or certify three passing repetitions/window-motion.

entries.title: Host application catalog and owned native sessions
entries.summary: Redeven owns host-user app discovery/authority/independent shares, without VM/container. Open admits sharing; last viewer closes transport, not app. Quit/force quit explicit. Linux recovery verifies identity, macOS uses OS inventory; missing capture never proves exit.

entries.title: Cross-platform host application behavior
entries.summary: Viewing, sharing, closing windows and ending processes are distinct on every OS. Ordinary actions preserve unsaved work and app cancellation; only confirmed Force quit bypasses saving. Backend facts drive supported controls. Session/display policy remains authoritative and unavailable recovery cannot silently relaunch.

entries.title: Linux application instances and independent sharing
entries.summary: Redeven owns Linux instances/shares; Floe Native Apps observes GIO/processes. Apps outlive viewers and Runtime. Recovery requires original user/state, kernel generation and endpoint, never PID alone. Reboot, display destruction or external cgroup cleanup may end apps.

entries.title: Client input for host applications
entries.summary: Floe remote-input owns keyboard/composition; clients own IME/preedit/candidates and hosts deliver confirmed Unicode/keys to painted windows. Each operation has one output owner. Binding loss cancels/releases without replay; old protocols require explicit save/quit/reopen.

entries.title: Pointer gestures for host applications
entries.summary: Floe owns swipe/tap/long-press gestures bound to painted window/generation. Cancel drops queued motion and releases buttons; remote-input owns composition. Missing capability requires explicit save/quit/reopen; closing viewer neither upgrades nor stops the application.

entries.title: Host application display and window layout
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps owns Linux display constraints/cursor coordinates; Redeven declares quality/layout and Desktop native window geometry. Receipts cannot loop resize; unchanged configuration preserves canvases. Old backends retain density with explicit limits, never automatic app restart.

entries.title: Native Linux host application picture streams
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps owns capture, region encoding and composition. Redeven presents preferences/measurements. Only composed pixels authorize input/ACK; quality changes retain process/connection identity. Malformed/incompatible frames need explicit recovery; surviving legacy sessions remain viewable under the display contract.

entries.title: Host application viewer resources and layered upgrades
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps owns immutable viewer documents/assets/digests/capabilities; Redeven pins one per authorized Xpra share. Compatible apps reconnect after updates without PID/content changes. Preparation failure exposes Retry; backends/modules retain lifetimes without hot swaps.

entries.title: Host application viewer state and recovery
entries.summary: Runtime/native events own app facts and bootstrap owns viewing. Decoded pixels precede input; transport loss never proves exit. Reconnect keeps process identity. Only confirmed final-window/app closure dismisses an established viewer; terminal pages remain readable and application/titlebar authorities stay separate.

entries.title: Host application platforms and initialization
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps owns Linux graphics/package/service adaptation; Redeven catalog/authority/instances/viewer. Private Wayland/Xwayland or explicit X11 Xpra needs no monitor/full desktop. Never switch backend on failure; Snap/Flatpak require installed capabilities/services.

entries.title: macOS application picture quality and delivery
entries.summary: Native helper owns encoding/resolution; viewer preferences/statistics. Decode current generation before ack. Quality/reconnect preserves app identity/permission/input. Unavailable video explicitly uses image transport with actual source reported; failures retain reconnect policy.

entries.title: Native macOS host applications
entries.summary: Redeven opens installed bundles as Runtime user. Trusted Desktop Local launches directly; remote capture binds actual selected windows/processes. Authorization gates operations/streams. Missing login/permissions blocks capture; disconnect preserves apps and exact-process recovery.

entries.title: macOS application window lifecycle
entries.summary: Native helper binds exact AX windows to process instances; capture does not define lifetime. Confirmed destruction alone starts last-window grace. Uncertain inventory/capture/transport retains session recovery and revokes stale input; Runtime preserves explicit end reasons.

entries.title: macOS application menu scope
entries.summary: Helper exposes single-app menus, removing Apple/cross-app branches before issuing handles. Titles stay literal; only enabled current leaves with verified ancestry execute. Stale actions preserve app/capture and errors. Inspect only on explicit action, never launch/first-frame.

entries.title: macOS application capture process ownership
entries.summary: One lazy Manager-owned Swift helper serves Runtime catalog/app/desktop sessions. Suspension affects selected capture only; identity/permission/input/credit/cleanup remain independent. Failure ends sharing, not apps; explicit reopen may restart under native validation.

entries.title: macOS application management and graceful quit
entries.summary: Redeven manages authorized app actions; OS owns liveness, apps saving/quit cancellation. Quit binds original process generation without force/retarget/assumed exit. Stale/unavailable targets retain sharing/errors; native sessions own capture/input/viewer closure independently.

entries.title: Prepare Linux hosts for native applications
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps prepares managed Wayland/Xwayland; Desktop may transfer verified offline archives. No monitor/full desktop is needed. Snap/Flatpak require installed services; missing prerequisites get guidance, never automatic security changes. Refresh after explicit admin preparation.

entries.title: Host application distribution validation
entries.summary: Historical Xpra checks qualify tested userspace only, not host policy. Current combined-backend/sandbox/product results belong to desktop/package validation. CPU translation, missing subscriptions and untested policy stay explicit; administrators follow setup contracts.

entries.title: Host application picture performance
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps owns capture/encoding/decoding; Redeven forwards and qualifies picture choices under the display contract. Measure pixels/bytes, preserve failed budgets and limit claims to measured scope. Results cannot certify video, WAN, physical displays or universal parity.

entries.title: Host application input validation
entries.summary: Real app receipts/saved bytes qualify client input, not dispatch or DOM focus. Upstream owns native/Xpra; Redeven verifies viewer/transport/launch/recovery and preserves existing resources. Simulated events cannot certify system candidates or physical mobile input.

entries.title: Linux desktop and package compatibility validation
entries.summary: Real processes, native input and saved files qualify the named platform/source. Floe Native Apps owns reusable graphics/package evidence; Redeven owns launch, viewing and recovery. Prototype success cannot certify the exact release, arbitrary applications, physical GPUs or untested desktop versions.

entries.title: Host application platform validation
entries.summary: Native installed-stack evidence qualifies only the listed userspace, Runtime, CPU and display matrix. Containers/translated CPUs prove no host boot, kernel, security policy or native hardware behavior. Missing permissions/subscriptions and untested targets remain unqualified.

entries.title: Host application cursor acceptance
entries.summary: Published Floe Native Apps owns cursor geometry. Acceptance independently checks decoded pictures, click receipts and physical OS pointer. CSS/page screenshots alone cannot prove pointer appearance; unavailable devices remain unqualified under the viewer contract.

entries.title: Host application lifecycle acceptance
entries.summary: Qualify process, window, decoded-frame and viewer facts independently. Only confirmed closure ends physical viewers; unavailable surfaces retain apps/recovery and revoke stale input. Keep OS differences and authorization boundaries explicit; results never certify arbitrary apps.

entries.title: Portable native Runtime binaries
entries.summary: Shared builder owns Runtime/Gateway terminal linkage: Linux runs on glibc/musl without host loader; Darwin requires matching Apple build. Missing tools fail preflight. Static LGPL Linux releases must include matching source/relink materials or publication fails.

entries.title: Desktop loopback Web Service access
entries.summary: Desktop loopback allocates random HTTP127.0.0.1 origin per Environment/forward; all traffic still uses protected Runtime route. Never dial directly, change interfaces/apps or fall back to unified proxy. Closing owner window/Environment removes gateway and authority.

entries.title: Web Service system-browser authorization
entries.summary: Runtime alone admits browser access to Desktop-private unified_proxy services. Single-use exact-forward/path entries become Host-only pf-<id>.localhost sessions. Keep bridge/browser/service credentials separate; failed admission opens nothing and desktop_loopback is excluded.

entries.title: Managed Web Service opening
entries.summary: Templates parse entrances; Runtime verifies/persists preparation; Desktop navigates and Env App presents. Open verified Host/Container/Compose entrances through Forward without lifecycle/data changes. HTTP401 proves availability only; failures offer recovery and never stop healthy apps.

entries.title: Managed Web Service Templates
entries.summary: Published redeven-service-templates owns definitions/releases/locales/icons/notices. Redeven embeds digest-verified offline bytes. Recommendations never constrain source or replace installs. Missing, malformed, mismatched or future bundles block startup without local fallback.

entries.title: Redeven Service Template format compatibility
entries.summary: Released templates own schemas/adapters/types; Runtime owns execution/authority. Old directories retain bytes/names/modes/digest/commit and adapt in memory to one executor. No stored duplicate definitions/lifecycle effects; invalid or unsupported formats fail unchanged.

entries.title: GitHub service template sources
entries.summary: Upstream acquires/validates templates; Redeven authorizes import/review/active pointer. Public/private GitHub import uses request-scoped credentials without git. No background updates or lifecycle effects; failure preserves active source and blocks only affected template.

entries.title: Independent Host service lifecycle
entries.summary: Apps own execution; Redeven owns authorized lifecycle/native identity/launch records/opening. Restart preserves PID/generation. No supervisor or PID-only authority. Distinguish absent/mismatched/uninspectable: only absence permits launch; opening failure never stops app.

entries.title: Managed Web Services
entries.summary: Redeven owns instances/resources/bindings/operations/forwards; verified templates define behavior. One engine serves Host/Container/Compose lifecycle. Registry and exact resource identity authorize actions; invalid provenance, ownership, permission or health never adopts unknown resources.

entries.title: Web Service management recovery
entries.summary: Registry owns lifecycle/transactions; Manager observes resources/actions; renderer shows current state/result/next step. Unavailable is not absent, failure history not current state. Destruction needs fresh ownership/consent; offline detach preserves resources and claims no stop.

entries.title: Service resource ownership
entries.summary: Registry records allocations/identity; fresh engine/filesystem checks establish facts. State roots receive independent default data/workspaces. Names and unverified legacy resources grant no deletion authority; uncertainty preserves review and upgrades never move live data.

entries.title: Managed Service operation progress
entries.summary: Manager Reporter owns live output; Registry owns history. One operation ID retains disclosure/completion through refresh. Redact command templates before storage; output grants no identity. Capture/storage/transport failures must not expose secrets, queries, private paths or control bytes.

entries.title: Managed Service release discovery and updates
entries.summary: Configured npm/OCI registries supply releases; Redeven validates identity/compatibility/update/rollback. Discovery only recommends; users select and explicitly install. Revalidate expiring candidate IDs at execution. Failure preserves healthy service and last-success facts without implicit mutation.

entries.title: Managed Service version interaction
entries.summary: Redeven presents one version-selection/submission drawer; Manager admits exact update plans. Preparation executes nothing; changed notices require consent. Failed preparation retains browsing/selection. Accepted work outlives drawer, with source failures actionable in place.

entries.title: Managed Service Instance Configuration
entries.summary: Verified template owns baseline; Redeven owns overrides, release/digest, resources, secrets and rebuilds. One resolver combines baseline/differences. Apply requires stopped state, current revision/plan/risk checks; failure preserves prior state or explicitly reports rollback failure.

entries.title: Runtime Service snapshot
entries.summary: Typed Runtime snapshots expose protocol/version, compatibility epoch, capabilities, readiness and workload identity to Desktop/Local UI. Gateway attachment is optional routing, never a prerequisite for independent access or authenticated host lifecycle management.

entries.title: Runtime session permission gates
entries.summary: Runtime validates session metadata and supported app/channel pairs before intersecting control-plane and local policy. Code App and Port Forward add their own gates. Read permits existing monitor/process observations; process termination independently requires execute and cannot inherit authority from visibility.

entries.title: Runtime system monitoring
entries.summary: Monitor owns one CPU/memory/network/process snapshot for page and Workbench. All OS-marked loopback interfaces are excluded from the shared network counters/rates. Failed network samples never enter history or fall back to unfiltered totals; later samples recover independently while other metrics remain usable.

entries.title: Runtime transport dependencies
entries.summary: Runtime composes Transport v3 and published Flowersec connection/session/RPC/stream primitives; Floeterm owns terminal lifecycle. Each Env App shares one current protocol session across RPC and live streams. Desktop SSH placement HTTP/2 is separate and does not redefine Flowersec wire or public SDK behavior.

entries.title: Runtime artifact spend and control pool
entries.summary: Opaque single-spend control/data artifacts bind each Lease to a digest-global tombstone. Persist idempotent bootstrap/top-up identities; reject stale, duplicate, malformed, expired or cross-environment responses. Replenishment/relink are explicit terminal transitions, never silent fallback.

entries.title: Runtime terminal lifecycle
entries.summary: Floeterm owns PTY/Ghostty VT, geometry/controller epoch, input encoding, history/reset and atomic Presentation. Redeven maps permission/session metadata/placement. Browser consumes bounded semantic streams without parsing bytes or introducing a second terminal state machine.

entries.title: Product RPC request encoding
entries.summary: Redeven codecs construct JSON; Flowersec validates/dispatches. File creation preserves empty content and omitted encoding; absent options stay omitted, explicit false/empty retain meaning. Invalid input fails before dispatch and needs codec repair, not retries or weaker validation.

entries.title: Git workspace inventory lifecycle
entries.summary: Git queries expose bounded immutable snapshots with revision-bound paging. Git/Files mutations coordinate topology and invalidate snapshots around effects; display grants no authority. Oversized/stale/malformed/exhausted reads return bounded typed errors without losing Flowersec session.

entries.title: Env App upstream web dependencies
entries.summary: Env App adapts published Floe UI/runtime/protocol, FloeBrowser projection, Floeterm terminal-web and Flowersec helpers. Manifest/lock pins define the consumed release; Floe owns asset monitoring and per-view recovery, while Redeven supplies authenticated product integration.

entries.title: Env App terminal and surface composition
entries.summary: Env App adapts Floeterm PTY facts and Floe shell, focus, selection and KeepAlive. Redeven owns views/localized controls. Session-keyed Runtime nodes survive view changes; visible panes paint independently while the active session owns input, search and commands.

entries.title: Env App connection and recovery
entries.summary: Env App binds published Floe artifact/connection contracts to exact origin/environment across HTTPS, explicit HTTP, Cloud and Desktop-private loopback. Require matching Service Worker control; Flowersec diagnostics form one immutable recovery view without replay or invented retry policy.

entries.title: Whole-window status surfaces
entries.summary: Floe owns window layout/retry/artwork; Redeven maps actual access/connection state. Opaque neutral recovery covers retained inert workspaces without duplicate notices. Floating windows/widgets/drag exclude this material; appearance grants neither authority nor another recovery loop.

entries.title: Env App page asset recovery
entries.summary: Floe compares assets/isolates views; Redeven supplies secure authenticated trigger, copy and explicit reload. Connected Runtime does not prove old modules usable. Import/build changes expose recovery within content; never reload over drafts or move native/shell controls.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin host integration boundary
entries.summary: Redeven consumes coordinated released ReDevPlugin Go/npm/Rust/machine artifacts. Product owns sessions, source review, placement, runtime builds and business adapters. Missing or unverifiable platform contracts fail without copied mechanics, sibling imports or compatibility fallback.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin 3.15 performance qualification
entries.summary:
ReDevPlugin 3.15.0 improves measured warm execution and Redeven restores only
initially visible plugin placements. Opened surfaces retain their independent
slots, drafts, selection and pending work when hidden. This is conditional lazy
opening, not a concurrency cap or iframe reuse. Platform mechanisms and release
ownership remain in [the host boundary](../architecture/redevplugin-boundary.md).

entries.title: ReDevPlugin Redeven adapters
entries.summary: Redeven binds authenticated sessions, source policy, business capabilities and placement to released ReDevPlugin. Platform alone owns protocol/trust/execution/state. Adapter faults stop at product boundary without implicit grants, copied platform state or substitute lifecycle.

entries.title: Plugin platform integration
entries.summary: Redeven mounts one released ReDevPlugin Host/HTTP namespace/client/scope. Published Supervisor runs verified Linux/Darwin runtime. Product supplies sessions, sources, placement and adapters; platform owns package/state/protocol/trust/execution. Unproven identity fails closed.

entries.title: Plugin process sessions
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin Process Broker owns processes; Redeven supplies authenticated scope/permission/minimal environment/secrets/state/audit. Opaque handles expose bounded binary stdio, no second protocol. Overflow may lose output; close/disable/uninstall/revoke/owner teardown stops owned work.

entries.title: Plugin background entries
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns headless Worker lifecycle and durable intervals. Redeven supplies environment permission policy and presents verified status through ordinary plugin management. No hidden surface, host scheduler, replay endpoint or second Worker protocol is involved.

entries.title: Plugin package and runtime lifecycle
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns trust, inspection, install, readiness, caches and durable lifecycle. Redeven supplies authenticated sources/review/localized outcomes. Every source requires inspection, explicit consent and released Host admission; stale/unverified/uncertain facts fail closed.

entries.title: Plugin surface recovery and permissions
entries.summary: Env App owns one authenticated plugin client, shared scope and installation observer. ReDevPlugin owns inventory, Executions, Events, permissions, revocation and recovery. Panel closure/reconnect retains exact request identity and outcome; refresh never becomes another mutation or lifecycle.

entries.title: Plugin market consumption
entries.summary: Redeven atomically refreshes validated latest-only market metadata for trusted Env App. Catalog identifies GitHub releases but hosts no packages or grants. ReDevPlugin verifies exact assets. Invalid refresh fails; last-good data permits stale discovery, never automatic updates.

entries.title: Native container operation observation
entries.summary: Every Containers mutation has one durable operation ID and resource lock in containerresource. Submission, progress, cancellation and restart reconciliation share that owner. Inventory/UI never create another lifecycle; stale plans, lost replies or unavailable engines remain explicit without automatic replay.

entries.title: Native container resources
entries.summary: Native Containers shares containerengine Docker/Podman execution with Web Services; containerresource alone owns mutations/state/reconciliation. Managed service resources are read-only here. Stale, unknown or uncertain facts fail closed without mutation replay.

entries.title: Container runtime execution
entries.summary: containerengine owns Docker/Podman discovery and execution. Each request binds engine, endpoint and canonical resource. Observe engines independently without probing inactive contexts or changing global selection. Failures stay explicit, never empty success or fallback; resource mutations retain their own admission owner.

entries.title: Volume usage observation
entries.summary: The engine supplies bounded volume observations to authenticated active Runtime resources. References include stopped containers and sizes mean occupied bytes, not capacity. Partial inspection proves no unused state. Failed size reads preserve inventory with unavailable metrics; mutations still require current preflight.

entries.title: Container engine service management
entries.summary: One ContainerServiceController owns Docker/Podman discovery, lifecycle, configuration, preflight identity and reconciliation. Opaque IDs hide endpoints; mutation requires full RWX/Admin without elevation. Unknown owner/revision/final state fails closed, never replaying interrupted work.

entries.title: Native container console
entries.summary: Containers console owns Activity/Workbench selection and navigation over authorized targets. Resource snapshots own shared inventory/refresh. Old-target replies cannot commit; UI has no endpoint selector, and containerresource remains the sole lifecycle mutation owner.

entries.title: Runtime access sessions
entries.summary: Runtime accessgate alone owns validity/revocation. Valid sessions survive tabs/refresh/disconnect; cookie names isolate protocols/ports without extra authority. Expiry/logout/security/restart needs login. Invalid/incompatible clients fail closed; MFA owns credential recovery.

entries.title: Runtime two-factor authentication
entries.summary: Runtime accessgate independently requires password then TOTP/recovery for browser/direct/Cloud sessions. Password challenges grant no app access. Native/SSH management has separate authority; missing/corrupt state fails closed and recovery blocks access until new credentials commit.

entries.title: Local UI network exposure
entries.summary: New Runtime endpoints explicitly use HTTP localhost:23998; network exposure retains local access and requires fixed port/effective password. HTTPS is separate with strict certificate/trust checks. Pages and WS/WSS share the public port. TLS failure never downgrades; private Desktop bridge cannot become public fallback.

entries.title: Local UI certificates
entries.summary: Runtime validates HTTPS identity; Desktop offers explicit create/import/regenerate/remove. Trust, validity and operation result differ. Never replace identity/install trust silently; invalid import retains pair and changes affect next HTTPS start, not sessions. HTTP needs no certificate.

entries.title: Permission policy and filesystem scope
entries.summary: Runtime policy is authoritative even after control-plane session authorization. Clamp grants by local permission policy and scope every file-facing feature to explicit directory roots. Product controls present that decision; they never widen permissions or infer access from paths.

entries.title: Plugin platform integration security
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin accepts authenticated host identity and source policy, never browser-claimed trust. HTTP checks auth/origin/CSRF/action; direct calls check owner/action/resource. Provenance, signatures, execution approval, update eligibility and permissions remain independent and fail closed on identity or scope mismatch.

entries.title: Verified Environment access routes
entries.summary: Desktop associates Gateway routes only through trusted attachment ID, Runtime public ID and Gateway-key matches; health is independent. Names/URLs/renderer claims grant nothing. Local/Cloud ownership stays separate; missing/unverified routes require explicit replacement.

entries.title: Host application component cache
entries.summary: Published artifactcache owns verification, locking and eviction. Desktop supplies its private directory, seven-day idle retention and 2 GB budget plus document-local transfers/UI. Devices reuse verified archives; cancellation retains completed cache. Unknown catalogs fail and cleanup cannot negate successful preparation.

entries.title: Desktop qualification lifecycle
entries.summary: Desktop supervisor owns scenario/resource/cleanup deadlines. Acceptance leaves no owned processes, bridges or fixtures; preserve production Quit and independent Runtime. Names/ports grant no stop authority. Timeout/interruption/forced cleanup/residue fails with retained manifest evidence.

entries.title: Desktop development sessions and bundles
entries.summary: Development launcher owns Desktop, local Runtime, saved Gateways and bundles. Launch exact current source and stop owned services together. Prune only verified inactive bundles, preserving user identity/data, unrelated services and recent/selected/live builds; incomplete inventory blocks pruning.

entries.title: Desktop Web Service browser window
entries.summary: Desktop owns protected target views, toolbar, navigation and cleanup over Runtime-authorized Web Service routes. Reopen reuses the same live forward; content gets no Desktop bridge. Invalid navigation rejects, while marked upstream failure offers local retry without reauthorizing or restarting the app.

entries.title: Desktop host application titlebar
entries.summary: Redeven owns the compact host toolbar; macOS capture/Xpra own commands and sessions, Desktop supplies native geometry. Window selection, picture settings and close share one titlebar. Disconnect disables unavailable actions while preserving window and recovery.

entries.title: Desktop shell theme state
entries.summary: One validated Desktop theme snapshot drives Welcome, Env App, chrome and generated documents. New/reset themes use Porcelain; valid choices survive upgrades. Selection paints before persistence, retaining acknowledged state, drafts/focus/content and Retry on failure.

entries.title: Desktop runtime bridge
entries.summary: Desktop opens independent Runtime through startup, scoped transport and sessions. Its process-local coordinator manages Local/WSL/SSH/container lifecycle; Gateway/Cloud remain routes. Observations never create competing owners; plugins use released brokers, not Desktop credentials.

entries.title: Desktop Environment library
entries.summary: Welcome projects authoritative owners into one library. Exact Runtime/Cloud links share a card; paired Gateways add access tabs. Independent registrations remain separate. Grouping grants no permission or fallback transport. Unlink restores cards; Cloud failures preserve known entries with stale-result context.

entries.title: Desktop interaction continuity
entries.summary: Welcome owns interaction sessions; Launcher/Runtime own business operations. Observations retain open panels, draft, focus, selection, steps and scroll. Only explicit user transitions or current completion alter visibility. Invalid authority blocks submission with recovery; closing progress never cancels work.

entries.title: Environment card presentation
entries.summary: Environment cards preserve geometry across perspectives, snapshots, narrow layouts and long translations. Each perspective selects an explicit route without granting authority or falling back. Snapshots retain nodes, selection and focus; owner removal invalidates submission but retains open sessions.

entries.title: Desktop Welcome navigation
entries.summary: Welcome page selection is immediate and independent of Launcher IPC or Runtime preparation. Visited pages retain state; readiness gates Flower requests, not navigation. Explicit Environment tab changes may animate cards, while refresh/return preserves headers and skips entrance replay.

entries.title: Desktop Environment connections
entries.summary: Welcome/settings derive connections from host access, placement, Runtime addresses and health. Presentation never selects transport; failed observations cannot prove exit. Keep host/container namespaces and private credentials distinct; explicit Stop clears addresses.

entries.title: Desktop runtime readiness
entries.summary: Managed Environments need exact-target compatible Runtime/Local UI readiness. Gateway/Cloud/URL access is separate. Missing/stopped/outdated/damaged Runtime offers direct recovery. Startup waits are bounded; retained diagnoses present state but current Presence owns authority.

entries.title: Runtime platform facts and icons
entries.summary: Runtime owns OS facts; Desktop renders trusted known values with bundled marks/localized names. Last-known facts survive disconnect/restart until replaced. Unknown OS uses a device mark without blocking Runtime; updates preserve geometry/focus and never infer OS from client identity.

entries.title: Desktop transport recovery
entries.summary: Each placement bridge owns HTTP/2, immutable recovery generation and registry identity. Its owner replaces stdio/session once, verifies process/Runtime, rejects late callbacks and disposes resources at one terminal boundary. Health observers or individual streams cannot independently restart transport.

entries.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations
entries.summary: Desktop uses saved SSH connection/placement for host/container Runtime. One local coordinator, operation, transport lease and temporary helper own lifecycle/recovery. Gateway/Cloud credentials grant no SSH authority; targets persist no Desktop supervisor or lifecycle lock.

entries.title: Desktop WSL runtime operations
entries.summary: Windows11x64 runs Electron, not native Local/container Runtime. Register initialized Linux x64 WSL2 targets; manage only exact distro/user Runtime. Windows owns distro lifecycle. Missing/old/uninitialized targets or broken commands/packages/Bridge need visible explicit recovery.

entries.title: Desktop session and model source
entries.summary: Desktop publishes explicit Environment route/identity. Accepted Stop/Restart/Update invalidates sessions. Each session has one process-local model-source owner for reconnect; startup never delays Env App and credentials stay local. Saved Flower history remains readable offline.

entries.title: Desktop Environment registration ownership
entries.summary: Each Environment action names its registration owner: Local, runtime target, saved URL or Gateway member. Linked cards never choose storage. Desktop serializes preference changes, publishes commits immediately and fences late probes/Open so removed records cannot return.

entries.title: Desktop environment settings
entries.summary: One settings window/session opens immediately per Environment. Registered identity resolves section/management authority; Runtime owns access config. Failures retain draft/diagnosis and late replies cannot replace new opens. Cloud/URL/Gateway never reads or saves Local access.

entries.title: Desktop environment settings presentation
entries.summary: Desktop composes Floe dialogs/tabs/controls into one bounded settings surface. Theme tokens own material, product CSS grouping/geometry. Every page retains readable labels, reachable actions and draft ownership through loading/errors/disclosure. Settings sessions retain authority and persistence without styling state.

entries.title: Desktop SSH environment settings
entries.summary: SSH creation/editing share one form and registration API. Common controls precede advanced options, retained in an inspectable summary. Failures preserve drafts. Registration contracts own connections/secrets, while Environment settings owns the window, tab, draft and asynchronous recovery lifetime.

entries.title: Desktop runtime process lifecycle
entries.summary: One RuntimeLifecycleCoordinator owns managed Local/WSL/SSH/container operations through saved direct channels. First admission retains the target until terminal; conflicts return its identity without preemption/queueing. Gateway/Provider grant access only, and old process or renderer state cannot create another owner.

entries.title: Desktop managed Environment reinstall
entries.summary: Wipe reinstall confirms exact target/root, verifies package, attempts stop, replaces root, verifies startup and cleans old data. Unknown process or broken state cannot block filesystem recovery. Preserve-data reinstall changes managed files and rolls back failed verification.

entries.title: Desktop application updates
entries.summary: One Desktop update coordinator serves every entry. Packaged macOS uses signed architecture-specific Sparkle; Linux uses matching DEB/RPM feeds. Unsupported, development or misplaced builds offer manual recovery. Internal Windows NSIS has no production update feed.

entries.title: Optional Runtime Cloud egress
entries.summary: Cloud is optional Runtime functionality. Gateway has no Cloud binding or credentials. A Runtime can explicitly select an attached Gateway as a restricted network exit; that selection changes transport, never Cloud ownership or independent access authority.

entries.title: Gateway device trust and host operations
entries.summary: Paired devices receive independent Gateway access, never accounts, roles or host-management grants. Scoped TLS bootstrap supports fresh private networks. Runtime password/MFA and Web Center administrator protection remain independent; revocation affects only the device's derived channels.

entries.title: Independent Gateway service
entries.summary: Gateway independently owns Runtime attachment/device admission/relay, working without Cloud account, cached authority or public Internet. Cloud alone owns membership/organizations/roles. Gateway device trust and Runtime environment authentication create no local user directory.

entries.title: Gateway network settings
entries.summary: Verified host admin atomically saves share endpoints/listeners/Host restrictions. Listener changes require explicit restart; live sockets persist. Empty hostname restrictions never weaken TLS/invitations/membership/Desktop policy. Invalid or failed writes preserve saved/live state.

entries.title: Gateway Desktop interactions
entries.summary: Desktop enrolls Local, SSH, WSL and container Runtimes through one app session. Management, invitation verification and consent are separate authorities; only confirmed membership completes enrollment. Observations retain drafts, failures require explicit recovery, and no Runtime URL enrollment form exists.

entries.title: Gateway access sessions
entries.summary: Desktop reaches joined Runtime over its outbound Flowersec Gateway connection; Gateway forwards to fixed application entry without dialing a Runtime URL. Desktop/Runtime terminate TLS; Runtime retains password/MFA/Host/Origin authority. Entry expiry never shortens established sessions.

entries.title: Independent Gateway qualification
entries.summary: Independent Gateway acceptance uses production handlers, host placements, real application authentication and multilingual management. Evidence qualifies only exercised device admission and revocation paths. UI/process qualification stays separate from exact-main push gates and release packaging.

entries.title: CodeSpace system-browser access
entries.summary: Desktop resolves trusted resource identity over Environment transport into short-lived loopback entry. Browser receives resource-bound HTTP/WS, never private bridge tokens. Runtime owns permission/editor generation; closing Environment retires routes and failed open leaves no listener.

entries.title: Native Desktop CodeSpace access
entries.summary: Desktop owns CodeSpace window/profile/loopback listener/route; Runtime owns editor generation/permissions/AccessGate. Native HTTP/WebSockets need no privileged preload. Close/revoke/stop ends connections; route or saved-port failure never substitutes transport or replays requests.

entries.title: Browser Editor runtime
entries.summary: Browser Editor support is owned by the Code App app server. Codespaces are opened through Local UI `/cs/<id>/` routes or through remote `cs-*` sandbox hosts, while Desktop and Env App can prepare or update managed Browser Editor runtime versions through code workspace engine APIs.

entries.title: Flower MCP runtime
entries.summary: Redeven configures MCP over official Go SDK stdio/Streamable HTTP sessions; Floret owns invocation/approval/effects/history/recovery. Add no competing execution or retry owner. Unknown outcomes are terminal without replay; invalid saved configuration remains unchanged.

entries.title: Flower Agent Plugins
entries.summary: Flower loads environment-scoped Agent Plugins1.0.0 Skills/MCP, separate from native .redevplugin SDK/packages/market. Redeven owns admission/distribution/configuration and Floret invocation/history. A manifest identifies a package, never grants execution or registers a market listing.

entries.title: Flower plugin catalog integration
entries.summary: Flower can consume an explicitly configured plugin directory without shipping or maintaining a default index. Runtime sources and user-managed sources use the same catalog reader and GitHub installation workflow. Catalog availability never owns installed plugin authority.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas
entries.summary: Tessiven maps services to Runtime cards, tinted groups and distinct external dependencies. Root connections give overview; focus reveals local relationships. Canvas owns pan/zoom while details remain selectable. Flower edits documents; the canvas progressively presents them without a parallel manual editor.

entries.title: Tessiven relationship summaries
entries.summary: Shared Tessiven projection summarizes group relationships: at most four collapsed patterns, one expanded pool overview and exact physical-node rows. Canonical endpoints, IDs and evidence remain unchanged. Search, filters and paging expose detail; missing visible endpoints suppress previews without substitutes.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas navigation and rendering
entries.summary: Floe owns layout, routing and viewport painting; Tessiven provides topology, controls and palette. Folding/filtering never rewrites documents. Canonical relationships remain inspectable while only the selected scope paints. Worker/data failures stay visible, retaining the last valid scene during ordinary view changes.

entries.title: Tessiven Flower replies
entries.summary: Canvas replies use a compact themed floating reader. Flower owns conversation/actions/feedback; Floe owns geometry/pointer/layers. Hide retains composer/conversation. Errors, approvals and Retry keep canonical Flower behavior without a separate canvas recovery path.

entries.title: Runtime settings
entries.summary: Env App owns settings destinations/drafts/API adapters; Floe reusable layout/navigation. Narrow/revisited panels retain usability, drafts and scroll. APIs authorize writes, never reader UI. Failure retains input; maintenance continues through its controller after explicit consent.

entries.title: Flower extensions
entries.summary: Shared Flower retains Skills/MCP/Plugins management through typed authenticated carrier adapters. The rail entry below New chat preserves drafts and tab filters; Runtime has no duplicate Skills destination. Readers inspect, admins configure, failures retain input/Retry, and all locales supply copy.

entries.title: UI presentation transactions
entries.summary: Navigation selects synchronously, paints intent, commits target visibility, then focuses/resizes/scrolls/measures after content paint. Floe owns visual/committed value separation; Redeven applies it across heavy product surfaces without duplicating business state.

entries.title: Env App floating layer order
entries.summary: Env App assigns global bands for windows, Flower, plugins, modals and commands; interaction reorders only its band. Floe owns viewport constraints/drag geometry. Redeven saves settled bounds while preserving reachable controls, local scroll and destination interaction.

entries.title: Dialog content placement
entries.summary: Published Floe owns Dialog structure; Redeven supplies localized content/actions. Headers hold identity/controls; guidance and consequences belong in bodies, including drawers and confirmations. Missing descriptions require content fixes, not hidden text or header subtitles.

entries.title: Adaptive desktop layout
entries.summary: Native Desktop keeps desktop interaction. Browser mobile mode requires width below 768 CSS px, coarse primary pointer and no hover; narrow mouse windows keep Activity/Workbench. Floe observes layout and owns drawer focus; Redeven owns navigation. Automatic placement preserves saved navigation and collapse choices.

entries.title: Mobile shell navigation
entries.summary: Redeven owns mobile navigation; Floe owns viewport, presence and focus. Mobile hides the framework toolbar behind a fixed More action while keeping bottom navigation reachable. Covered content stays inert through exit, confirmations remain modal, and closing navigation preserves content and admitted operations.

entries.title: File preview window actions
entries.summary: Redeven owns file actions/drafts; Floe titlebar/window lifecycle. Compact actions precede window controls in Activity/Workbench, preserving permission/selection/download/discard policy. Close immediately fences pending work but keeps content visible through retirement.

entries.title: File preview dismissal
entries.summary: The preview owner cancels reads immediately; Floe owns exit presence. Accepted close retains document/title through motion and releases resources at unmount, without blank iframes, brighter intermediate surfaces, extra reads or delays. Disposal always cleans up and late responses cannot revive closed content.

entries.title: File preview viewport and rendering
entries.summary: Redeven owns preview identity/modes; Floe sizing, PDF layers and static PPTX. Initial fit may enlarge, resize keeps manual zoom. One owner renders each page, fencing stale work. Errors stay local/retryable, cancellation neutral, and incomplete HTML never executes.

entries.title: Static PPTX file preview
entries.summary: Floe parses/renders static PPTX; Redeven authorizes bytes and presents the reading surface. Local windowed slides retain text selection and zoom, with external resources disabled. Stale work cannot replace current source. Errors expose bounded recovery, and redistribution retains licenses and corresponding MPL source.

entries.title: HTML file preview
entries.summary: Redeven classifies files and authorizes reads/edits/placement; Floe constructs isolated HTML pages. Opening renders by default and source editing is explicit/write-authorized. Content cannot reach trusted Shell/resources. Oversized, incomplete or unreadable input never executes and retains localized recovery.

entries.title: Git workspace generation and Files decoration
entries.summary: Git projections bind protocol client/repository/revision. Changes, Branches and Files own state with shared monotonic invalidation. Files renders immediately, retaining decorations during bounded refresh; stale replies cannot restore invalid state, including after unknown effects.

entries.title: Shared surface material
entries.summary: Published Floe owns material and motion. Env App/Welcome select soft-neumorphic roles while business content stays flat. Preserve input, portals, widget identity and hot interaction ownership. Resolve conflicts at the product override source without copying shadow logic or introducing another theme/dependency owner.

entries.title: Product accessibility for AI agents
entries.summary: Redeven owns accessible names/state/relationships while preserving layout, handlers, focus and inert exclusion. Floe owns reusable controls/layers. Shared defects require evidence and published fixes. Scope claims accurately: accessibility edits alone certify neither WCAG nor model performance.

entries.title: Input focus boundaries
entries.summary: Published Floe owns focus presentation; Redeven supplies layout, semantic state and explicit compound-input boundaries. Ordinary fields change border color only, preserving geometry/shadows; the persistent Flower chat composer keeps its border unchanged. Fix conflicting styles at their owner with source/browser checks; no fallback stylesheet.

entries.title: Git browser visual states
entries.summary: Git selection and diff share a contained surface with independent request owners. Floe accent marks selection; semantic colors identify Git facts. Checked-out and inspected branches remain distinct when coincident. Retain local scrolling, keyboard and current diff across themes/widths.

entries.title: Git diff request lifecycle
entries.summary: One Git panel binds preview/full reads to target/revision/transport/mode. Stale replies cannot replace current content; unchanged placement retains request/content/scroll/expansion. Missing transport waits for Shell, while empty/error states settle explicitly without automatic retry.

entries.title: Workbench interaction contracts
entries.summary: This is the navigation point for explicit Workbench input and surface ownership. Focused concepts define wheel, pointer, text, terminal, selection, recovery, loading and overlays. Keep those responsibilities distinct rather than introducing widget-specific event heuristics.

entries.title: Workbench composition surfaces and editing
entries.summary: Floe owns composition rendering/editing/materials/anchored tools; Redeven locales/defaults/layout storage. Preserve native caret/selection/IME and optional empty region names. Save/reopen retains content/color/geometry/material; failed upgrade keeps prior supported layout.

entries.title: Workbench input ownership
entries.summary: Explicit markers distinguish canvas zoom, local scroll, pointer actions and text selection. Selected widgets do not automatically own wheel input; regions declare their role. Workbench preserves predictable canvas behavior alongside native nested product interactions.

entries.title: Workbench terminal interaction
entries.summary: Floeterm terminal-go owns PTY, VT, geometry, controller epoch, semantic history and atomic Presentation. terminal-web renders one canvas/view and collects local input. Authority/renderer faults fail closed; history/search faults stay local and retryable without disconnecting output.

entries.title: Terminal fonts across client devices
entries.summary: Env App owns document-local terminal fonts. New preferences use bundled JetBrains Mono at size 12; existing IDs/sizes remain unchanged and each client resolves availability. Floeterm retains canonical cells, cursor and session grid. Font presentation cannot replace terminal authority or erase stored preferences.

entries.title: Terminal session groups
entries.summary: Runtime catalogs own groups, assignments and named views; Activity/Workbench share environment projection with local expansion/active view. Default is immutable and every session has one known group_id. Membership is independent of placement, cwd, controller and recovery.

entries.title: Official installation progress
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns durable official-install Execution, progress and recovery. Redeven presents exact review/permission setup and retains work after management closes. Lost replies cannot reinstall; only current inventory exposes launch, and failed setup preserves saved layout.

entries.title: Plugin package review
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns package inspection, validation and atomic changes. Redeven presents exact source/candidate/permissions for consent. Cancel stops only pre-submit inspection; unknown effects reconcile without replay. Updates preserve layout with fresh slots; only confirmed uninstall removes it.

entries.title: Plugin layout continuity
entries.summary: Redeven persists exact widget/instance/surface geometry; ReDevPlugin owns authority. Upgrade/disable/permission/reconnect errors retain placement. Only explicit removal or confirmed exact uninstall deletes. Unknown outcomes reconcile without moving canvas or recreating authority.

entries.title: Workbench surface lifecycle
entries.summary: Workbench retains widget identity through selection/loading/recovery; Floe owns Dock focus. Selected Terminal viewports own wheel without DOM focus; unselected remain Canvas-owned. Shell recovery makes retained content inert in shared overlay layers without another visibility store.

entries.title: File icon presentation
entries.summary: Floe owns filename recognition, SVG icons and palettes; Redeven supplies names, directory/link metadata and size. Formats retain reviewed distinctions and unknown files use the generic upstream icon. Icons confer no preview/execution/extraction authority, whose independent format and permission checks remain.

entries.title: Files context menus
entries.summary: Floe owns file-menu placement, scrolling, gestures and dismissal; Redeven supplies bounds/actions/locales. Keep menus eight CSS pixels inside Files/surface/visible viewport intersection. Invalid bounds close; never escape global layers or duplicate Workbench transforms.

entries.title: Plugin Center interaction
entries.summary: Redeven owns Plugin Center navigation; Floe owns dialogs, presence and input. Workbench uses a retained drawer and Activity the same directory page. Search/filter/selection/scroll persist. Closing management does not cancel Host execution; released ReDevPlugin owns lifecycle, permissions and surface authority.

entries.title: Plugin surfaces
entries.summary: Redeven owns plugin discovery, navigation and placement; ReDevPlugin owns admission, surface authority, bridge sessions, confirmation and revocation. Activity/Workbench use independent SDK slots. Management retains search/selection and reconciles unknown outcomes against authoritative state.

entries.title: Flower thread Goals
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical Goal, model tool, reflection and completion; Redeven authorizes and presents facts. One current Goal/thread states intent without text limits or Todo dependency. Stop/navigation/recovery remain usable; unresolved requests never imply successful mutation.

entries.title: Flower command and composer flow
entries.summary: Each input has one retry-stable request ID echoed with ThreadID. New-thread HTTP nests it under create; existing uses client_request_id with URL thread. Short-lived nonsecret outbox retains uncertain input/settings while composer, Stop, navigation and interactions stay usable.

entries.title: Flower Activity origin page references
entries.summary: New desktop companion captures removable origin context without reads/editor replacement; existing threads do not. New chat/open with no selection refreshes; later edits/navigation do not. Submission uses exact visible text; terminal captures current screen, excluding unauthorized/unloaded facts.

entries.title: Flower conversation references
entries.summary: The composer owns unadmitted references; Floret owns admitted snapshots. Reference appends basic facts without sending or disturbing selection. Identity includes Runtime and Open requires authorized reads. Failed/canceled reads retain draft/preview; transport retries keep the frozen source even after rename/deletion.

entries.title: Flower composer references
entries.summary: Redeven owns authorized discovery and connection-local drafts; Floret owns admitted ordered references. Chips show files, directories, frozen threads/page context. Stale discovery retains editor; failed capture retains outbox without overwriting edits. Labels grant no identity or authority.

entries.title: Flower input history
entries.summary: Canonical Floret/cache text feeds Floe transient navigation and shared drafts. Unmodified ArrowUp in exactly empty chat recalls editable text, never submits. IME/selection/menus/structured answers keep keys; scope or external-draft changes stop browsing without losing text.

entries.title: Absolute filesystem directory selection
entries.summary: Floe owns picker navigation/validity/request lifetime; Redeven supplies authoritative path context/connection/locales/form. Absolute paths and root shortcuts grant no access. Failed navigation retains intent, disables confirmation and offers Retry; execution rechecks policy.

entries.title: Floating Files window dismissal
entries.summary: Files controller owns active request and immediate return focus. Floating host retains title/key/live browser through Floe exit presence, with no extra timer/copied content/second browser. Floe makes exit inert and disposes after motion, including reduced motion. New requests cancel exit through that same lifecycle.

entries.title: Personal directory favorites
entries.summary: Runtime stores independent ordered favorites/revisions per authenticated namespace/endpoint/user. Env App/Desktop supply metadata to published Floe pickers and menus; existing filesystem navigation alone validates/selects paths. Favorites neither grant authority nor duplicate navigation.

entries.title: Flower working directory navigation
entries.summary: Flower owns draft/thread directory intent; Env App destination navigation. Full-page selects/browses directory, companion omits it. Menus freeze thread/path. Activity opens Files/new Terminal; Workbench creates widgets without scaling canvas or injecting existing-shell commands.

entries.title: Flower mobile navigation
entries.summary: Shared mobile Flower opens a bottom list drawer over retained detail. Floe owns focus/presence/motion and scroll-preserving return. Draft/selection/DOM/header remain stable; covered detail stays inert and cannot acknowledge reads until exit under the shared adaptive contract.

entries.title: Flower Activity companion
entries.summary: Env App retains one Flower tree/stream across Activity, companion and available Workbench widget. Floe owns shell; Redeven placement/focus/read acknowledgement; Floret conversation. Moving placement or canvas selection never creates another product surface or lifecycle.

entries.title: Ask Flower window boundaries
entries.summary: Redeven places Ask Flower in Activity, Workbench and Welcome beneath visible Shell/native chrome. Header/composer stay reachable during drag and resize; maximize and titlebar double-click are unavailable. Floe constrains shrinking viewports while retaining the same composer, draft and interaction state.

entries.title: Flower companion composer and motion
entries.summary: One native textarea survives collapsed/expanded Flower with draft, selection, focus and IME intact. Redeven owns content; Floe shell geometry/motion. Expanded text sits above bottom toolbar/More; phase-driven close/reversal never remounts or adds lifecycle timers.

entries.title: Flower companion presence
entries.summary: Collapsed Flower uses canonical summaries/current-run detail from existing stream, prioritizing work, decisions and drafts. Historical completion is not new feedback. Presence never expands or acknowledges reading; Activity companion owns placement/focus/dismissal.

entries.title: Flower read state
entries.summary: Redeven confirms reads per user from server version and actual local presentation. Old responses cannot restore already-cleared indicators; unseen activity stays unread. Temporary sync failures recover in background without blocking operations or inventing acknowledgements.

entries.title: Flower incremental live state
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical history/versions; Redeven authorizes one workspace stream into ThreadCache. UTF-8 growth changes only its item. Transport/window recovery preserves execution, prose and drafts; retained DOM and scoped reads keep navigation/disclosure stable without rescanning history.

entries.title: Flower file edit preparation
entries.summary: Flower exposes candidate filenames during file-edit argument generation through existing display-only Floret previews. One stable row survives approval/execution; actual results alone prove completed edits. Progressive names explain long preparation without creating effect facts.

entries.title: Flower timeline ordering
entries.summary: Flower renders Floret ordered facts using stable item, TurnID and RunID identities. Captured ordinary input appears immediately; only that draft is consumed. Queued inputs stay in the dock. Canonical request-key confirmation preserves mounted rows without duplicates, and summaries never author timeline detail.

entries.title: Flower turn status and process disclosure
entries.summary: Floret owns turn outcome and timing. Terminal turns fold eligible process rows once; pending controls, uncertain effects and inspected work remain visible. Explicit choices persist, user messages/finals stay mounted, and settled question/answer receipts reopen with complete content.

entries.title: Flower reasoning selection ownership
entries.summary: Threads display confirmed reasoning independently of view revisions; new drafts retain explicit choices. Default means configuration, not On/guessed effort. Verified capabilities alone determine controls. Failed saves retain confirmed state and active turns keep frozen execution settings.

entries.title: Flower personal conversation preferences
entries.summary: Explicit model, directory and model-owned reasoning choices are remembered per authenticated namespace, endpoint and user. Loading/switching threads never writes defaults. New roots prefer explicit launch/draft choices, then personal memory, then configuration; existing threads and immutable turns retain confirmed settings.

entries.title: Flower model and navigation presentation
entries.summary: Flower separates Desktop/environment sources, unavailable models and first setup. Thread-owned model/reasoning choices remain authoritative. Navigation distinguishes visual intent from committed content and fences stale reads. Transient action failures use notifications; canonical failures remain in their timeline.
