sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Admission and serialization
The operation key contains engine, opaque endpoint ID, resource kind, and canonical identity.

Reusing a request ID with different hashes produces an idempotency conflict instead of a second operation.

## Execution, cancellation, and events
The service owns an operation context from queued state through reconciliation. Cancellation is an explicit API action; closing Activity, Workbench, an inspector, an event stream, or the browser never implies cancellation.

Terminal errors use a small public taxonomy for storage, registry availability, rate limiting, not-found, and access denial; the drawer maps known codes to localized guidance alongside the durable timeline. Unknown codes use a localized generic failure; codes and backend messages remain diagnostic evidence, not visible UI copy. Timeout guidance acknowledges that host work may still be in progress. Desktop service cards direct users to its native application for setup/startup recovery and expose status revalidation. Service history shows state transitions without generic execution stages or a synthetic percentage bar.

## Authoritative terminal observation
After engine execution returns, the service reloads the exact endpoint-bound resource or relevant bounded inventory.

The operation is never replayed, regardless of whether the resource appears present or absent.

## UI observation
Inventory requests and streams are fenced by source runtime, endpoint, resource view, and request generation. A superseded response cannot replace current data.

Mobile and desktop expose the same state and cancellation authority. Service lifecycle feedback stays on its card; history is secondary. Polling terminal transitions refresh authoritative service/runtime facts even when the event stream was lost. The portaled history drawer owns its responsive container and independent scrolling. Desktop uses a history sidebar; narrow drawers place a horizontal history strip above details. Rows use stable operation IDs and pressed selection; polling preserves focus and detail nodes. Details separate identity, live cancellation, duration/current health and timeline. The active final timeline step uses a pending indicator, never a completed check.

Cross-database atomicity is never assumed or simulated by copying upstream lifecycle state into Redeven tables.

Local session issuance declares only Env App API and plugin API paths plus the plugin CSRF and expected-management-revision headers. Remote issuers must declare the same plugin request authority and upload cap in their signed scope.

Product code must not reset a successful response while its bytes are still being consumed.

Flower maintains one workspace stream; thread selection never reconnects it.

Its transport and cancellation regression coverage remain intact.

The viewer's `WindowTransport` maps product paths into the published `flowersec-proxy/http1` and `flowersec-proxy/ws` stream APIs.

Acquisition requires read, write and execute permissions and an active resource owned by the authenticated user. Its exact spend target identifies the window kind, environment, port-forward application and forward ID; launcher, Runtime and application origins must all match.

A view-only session keeps the full access requirement.

Carrier failure clears the cached proxy runtime.

HTTPS or a trustworthy local origin is still required where the browser restricts those APIs; product code does not mark an insecure network origin as trustworthy.

concepts.title: Cross-platform host application behavior
concepts.summary: Viewing, sharing, closing windows and ending processes are distinct on every OS. Ordinary actions preserve unsaved work and app cancellation; only confirmed Force quit bypasses saving. Backend facts drive supported controls. Session/display policy remains authoritative and unavailable recovery cannot silently relaunch.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
| Operation | macOS | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Close outer Desktop window / browser popup | Release this client lease; app survives | Same |
| Network loss, reload, second viewer | Reconnect same live app; stale input is revoked | Same |
| Release this client lease | End this capture/route; other clients and app survive | End this proxy/route; other clients and app survive |
| No window for more than 40 seconds | Waiting, with native menu/reopen | Waiting, reconnect same process without relaunch |
| Close last window | Viewer closes; app decides whether its process exits | Same |
| Cancel normal close/quit | Preserve application and save dialog | Same; ordinary control is Close all windows |
| Explicit Force quit in library | Confirm loss warning; exact AppKit instance | Confirm loss warning; exact owned backend and descendants |
| Orderly Runtime shutdown or process exit | Native app remains discoverable | Private display survives; new Runtime verifies/reconnects it |
| Running list | Regular apps in the logged-in OS session | Caller-owned Redeven instances, including detached/windowless apps |
| Host reboot / display server destruction / OS cleanup | No survival guarantee | Same; Runtime cgroup cleanup may also end its virtual display |

## Accepted operations and visible state
Quit and force-quit requests are asynchronous. The Host Applications surface must close the confirmation dialog after acceptance and show a per-application pending state until the authoritative running snapshot confirms the target instance is gone.

The first Force quit action only enters that state; only its final confirmation sends the destructive host request.

sections.body: Linux cannot generically request AppKit-style application quit or reopen, nor adopt an arbitrary process on another display. macOS requires its real logged-in graphical session and explicit capture/input permissions. Neither backend can preserve an application after its OS or display environment has been destroyed.

Host launches in its own session and process group. The foreground start contract remains: templates must not double-fork, background the application, or retain a permanent wrapper.

The `host:v3` identity binds service ID, launch nonce, PID, and a digest of native facts:

New identities never use formatted dates, timezone, command text, or `kern.boottime`.

Host supplies verified native launch identity and executes only the applied authorized hooks through the common [managed opening contract](managed-web-service-opening.md). sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
`localui.Server` is built with an agent, Code App app server, bind spec, runtime-control socket path, Local Environment identity, diagnostics store, and optional access gate.

Local UI bind parsing accepts `localhost`, canonical loopback IP literals, concrete non-loopback unicast IPv4 and IPv6 literals, and the `0.0.0.0` and `::` wildcards.

In-process maps retain only active-session cleanup projections and never authorize a request.

## Concurrent shutdown
Context cancellation and explicit shutdown enter the same serialized close path. Runtime-control and management status serialize start/close and protect endpoint reads, so overlapping shutdown cannot dereference cleared servers or advertise a retired control listener. This uses bounded in-process locks and does not introduce durable lifecycle state.

## Session event observation
All built-in Env App event subscriptions use the current authenticated Flowersec session's HTTP proxy. Short bootstrap requests and native file/media requests stay independent of session acquisition.

Native applications and their unsaved work survive this shutdown.

## Resolution and picture controls
Capture dimensions use the smaller of the viewer's device-pixel ratio, the native window's pixel density, and the chosen longest-edge limit.

Opening settings never resizes the app.

Limits are bounded and validated by the native helper.

## Encoders and delivery
A browser advertising H.264 WebCodecs software decoding can receive VideoToolbox hardware video. Hardware encoder unavailability uses JPEG images; a browser decoder failure explicitly renegotiates image transport.

Unchanged resize requests retain frame credit.

## Observable statistics and limits
Runtime diagnostics record connection-to-first-frame duration and generation; the browser debug log measures connection-to-first-decoded-frame duration.

High latency, host capture, encoding, browser decoding and network capacity can reduce achieved frame rate; a 60 FPS limit is not a guarantee of 60 FPS delivery.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Waiting and process lifetime
A running process without its first shareable window remains attached indefinitely; there is no first-window termination deadline. Releasing the current client lease during this wait ends that sharing lease normally; missing pixels do not turn a lease release into a launch failure. An unexpected helper exit is a failed sharing session, not evidence that the host application ended.

## Window evidence
The window registry distinguishes present, unknown and confirmed-empty inventories. No first-window deadline is introduced.

## Capture and recovery
Capture availability is independent of lifetime. AX identity survives a capture-surface replacement while the input generation is renewed; retired callbacks cannot update the replacement. Failure to launch and unexpected helper loss remain failures; missing pixels do not change a confirmed process exit into a failed launch.

## Terminal state
Terminal state retains the native end reason: `application_exited` confirms the bound process exited, `windows_closed` confirms its last shared window closed, and `sharing_stopped` confirms detachment. Closing windows and stopping sharing never claim the process has quit. The [lifecycle validation matrix](../operations/host-application-lifecycle.md) separates automated recovery evidence from OS/application compatibility limits.

## Reporter and persisted detail
ManagedOperationProgressDetail schema v2 alone owns detail. Duplicate command IDs get deterministic suffixes. Failed uninstall retains records/output for [reviewed recovery](service-management-recovery.md).

## Service-row interaction
Page state keys disclosure by operation_id, never component/service-object identity. Rejected submissions retain local safe failure without backend operation or observed-state change. Compact status opens explicitly; failure labels/notices survive settlement and dismissal. Reduced motion removes animation, not readable completion hold.

## Execution panel
Published Floe planes, ink, LinearProgress, StableText and presence compose a connected rail and fixed-height panel. Narrow rail reveals its current step without scrolling the page. Open details show commands/output immediately in one scrolling transcript; no secondary disclosure. Logs/transfer/stage changes preserve neighboring geometry and existing output nodes. Preserve canonical interleaved output order; follow only while already at the end.

Restrained transitions retain progress identity. Reduced motion is static. Open is natively disabled during operations with its ordinary icon and keyboard/touch/hover action-stage tooltip.

TemplateSpec 7 accepts exactly one entrance source: a fixed endpoint path, the supported Host opening hook, or `startup_url.line_prefix`. Container and Compose never acquire permission to run Host scripts.

Update installs/verifies, resolves final installed metadata into one digest, replaces the process and health-checks before commit. Launch/journal/registry share the final digest; enriched trust creates no false pending changes. Originally stopped services return to stopped after verification. Failure retains rollback/recovery.

## Image pull feedback
Container pulls publish the executed command and ordered output through the existing operation reporter, including success, failure and cancellation. The reporter owns redaction and the 400-line/128-KiB output bound. Transfer rate derives from observed downloaded bytes over a short time window, retains the previous sample across sparse updates and decays when subsequent observations show no download. Layer completion is independent of byte progress.

concepts.title: Plugin background entries
concepts.summary: ReDevPlugin owns headless Worker lifecycle and durable intervals. Redeven supplies environment permission policy and presents verified status through ordinary plugin management. No hidden surface, host scheduler, replay endpoint or second Worker protocol is involved.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
A plugin may declare runtime_start, on_demand or interval. The first two use the platform background manager: starts are idempotent, scoped to the installed instance and environment, and independent of visible Activity or Workbench surfaces. Interval requires background.method.v1 and background.interval.v1, an explicit method and parameters, an environment-scoped job Worker, synchronous execution, no confirmation or preflight, a 1,000–86,400,000 ms period, and a 1–300,000 ms execution budget not exceeding the period.

The platform persists and claims each due invocation before dispatch. One instance runs at most one interval invocation; separate plugins remain independent. The first run waits one period, then each next run follows completion plus the period. Missed periods coalesce. Restart preserves completed plans; an unfinished claim becomes unknown and is never replayed. A later period is new work, not proof of the earlier result. Disable, uninstall, package replacement and revocation fence and cancel exact current work. Host close drains execution before closing state. ReDevPlugin owns contiguous control-store migration and unknown-outcome handling.

Redeven's background policy snapshots the validated runtime LocalMax intersected with the Env App application cap, then applies the existing method-effect rules. It does not depend on an online session, borrow a user's cached authority, or apply a per-user override to an environment-owned job. Admin and unknown effects are denied. The platform separately verifies owner, installed package trust, current grants, revisions, runtime admission and the durable claim. This policy grants no filesystem, process, secret or network resource: adapters requiring a live user session continue to reject background access. Selected-file and connection approvals retain their existing lifetime and owner rules.

An explicit install/enable action authorizes the declared environment lifecycle through the ordinary product review and platform APIs. Permission removal blocks future dispatch without changing the user's enabled intent. The existing disable action stops work. No separate scheduling switch is introduced.

sections.title: Presentation
sections.body: Installation review shows the localized cadence for interval entries. Method identity, exact period and execution budget remain inside existing expandable technical details. Installed details consume the authoritative background_interval projection: scheduled, running, stopped or blocked, with next-run time only while scheduled. A prior failed or unknown result remains visible without a retry button that could replay effects. A previous background diagnostic cannot override current interval status; separate process diagnostics remain available. Refresh uses the existing owner-scoped inventory path.

See [Plugin platform integration](plugin-platform-integration.md), [Plugin process sessions](plugin-process-sessions.md), and [ReDevPlugin boundary](redevplugin-boundary.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- `internal/redevpluginintegration` passes an explicit state root and core, official-release, runtime, connectivity, secret, capability and external-package modules. External sources use bounded public HTTPS, GitHub Release resolution and upstream signature assessment.
- Session close uses the released durable four-hash coordinator; remove authentication only after exact drain acknowledgement. Process-local connection generations cancel replaced waits and reject late credentials.
- Shutdown closes Local UI admission/hijacked transports, cancels Agent sessions, drains request leases/handlers, then invokes idempotent Host teardown.
- [Package lifecycle](redevplugin-package-lifecycle.md), [process sessions](plugin-process-sessions.md), [background entries](plugin-background-entries.md) and [surface recovery](redevplugin-surface-recovery.md) own their detailed contracts.
- Runtime binds the canonical sibling executable, target, released IPC/WASM ABI, exact product build, lease replay storage and limits. [Native container resources](container-resources-capability.md) owns the separate product container capability.
- Activity targets receive fresh SDK slots in stable Shell-root windows; responsive chrome cannot remount/adopt iframes. Workbench uses projected plugin widgets. Lost close responses reconcile through exact-surface authority; disposal alone is not revocation.

## Ordinary Web placement

A surface opens through the released Web SDK using an origin prepared by its product transport. The same package can use browser-native HTML, CSS, ES modules, Canvas and WebGL without a product renderer. Each simultaneous placement owns its own iframe and slot. Desktop and browser child-origin requests cannot access product management routes or borrow the parent's private bridge token.

Pure Web applications can declare their own private resources and call the
released KV, database, file and settings SDK directly. Product routes forward
resource requests without replacing the platform's Surface/session checks or
buffering binary bodies into a product protocol. Public actions stay on the
existing bridge and Execution/Event contract; backend or background work uses
the released Worker lifecycle. File uploads use atomic staging, and snapshot
watches coalesce intermediate changes. Neither implies zero-copy or a change log.

sections.body:
## Ownership and isolation
Every session binds plugin instance, user scope, environment scope, plugin invocation/session, and client key. Start requests contain an executable and argv array; ReDevPlugin never parses an implicit shell command string.

Secret references are resolved by the Host adapter and values do not cross the UI, error, audit, or diagnostic projections.

For one owner and client key, ReDevPlugin reuses only a field-equal launch request. It snapshots argument and environment collections before starting; later caller mutations cannot redefine an in-flight or running launch. Changed launch fields return a launch-conflict error. Redeven delegates this decision to the platform.

## Streams and lifecycle
The first contract supports non-PTY stdin, stdout, and stderr only. Each output stream has an independent cursor and bounded ring buffer.

The platform removes the session after close and prevents access after owner revocation.

## Ownership
Upstream owns validation/hash/trust, inspection/registry, permission/confirmation, tokens/assets, sandbox/bridge, settings/intents, Executions/Events, storage/network/secrets, supervision/IPC/WASM, quotas/revocation, control state and releases/contracts. [Packages](redevplugin-package-lifecycle.md) owns admission/cache, [adapters](redevplugin-redeven-adapters.md) product modules/display.

## Availability
Plugin readiness cannot block Runtime/ordinary sessions. Market/package/runtime/storage/init failure stays local; retain files/terminal/Notes/Workbench. PLUGIN_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE executes nothing; rejected writes report not_committed. Localize faults; unreadable inventory is not empty, auto-failure never global interruption. Init budget10s; cancel fences results/closes integration. Error/panic unwinds construction without hiding host cancellation.

Channel auth is separate: failed/panicked binding grants nothing and cannot close host channel. Request panic releases admission; HTTP contains failure. Incompatible opaque state stays unchanged, never reauthorized.

## Network/history
ReDevPlugin3.12.0 separates routing/package verification/execution. Single-hop host transports honor explicit proxy,current macOS proxy/PAC,OS DNS/VPN for market/package/release. Synthetic/private addresses alone are not denial. Upstream validates URL/redirect/origin/size/cancel/hash/signature; downloads grant nothing.

Granted HTTPS hostname connectors without private-prefix binding use released transport factory. Platform checks target/method/grant/revision,pools/quotas/revocation. Private prefixes,literal addresses/other protocols keep address-bound policy. Resolve configuration at request time; faults local.

3.11.2 reads signed pre-Webv9 without changing manifest/hash/signature/generation. Incompatible install stays manageable,not executable/enabled. Explicit same-install Web update retains history; no VNode/invented declarations. Unknown/corrupt stays unchanged/local unavailable.

Platform owns Web admission/package modules/sandbox/bootstrap/bridge. Product allocates origins/mounts handlers; no DOM translation/VNode renderer/ambient parent credentials.

## Runtime performance boundary
Released 3.15 uses one Wasmtime actor/job path with fresh invocation state, bounded in-process compiled-module reuse, finite fuel and signed deadlines. Immutable manifest caching never replaces current permission or revocation checks. Product supplies fixed toolchain, runtime signing and placement policy; it does not add an executor, authorization cache or compatibility fallback. Cold module preparation remains separate from warm execution latency.

## Authoring/execution
Platform owns config/manifest validation,bindings,build/test/package,diagnostics/watch,persistent preview,manual update candidates,connection review,verified dev runtime. Redeven version-derived skill invokes released CLI. Product owns intent/placement/review/install approval and build/signature/SBOM/publication proof; authoring grants no permissions/trust.

3.13.0 owns manifest actions/direct Surface KV/SQLite/files/settings without Worker forwarding. Dedicated-origin binary/WebSocket handler requires exact handshake; Host checks session ceilings/scope/grants/quotas/revoke. Product mounts/presents,never new endpoints/manifest interpretation. SDK conflict/unknown cannot replay; coalesced watches are not logs.

Private files1→chunked2 migration stays upstream, separate from control/author schemas. Snapshots/recovery opaque; no copied SQL/rewrite.3.12.2 retains ordinary packaging/SDK. Trusted parent query/event/cancel binds current surface gateway/plugin; pass exact scope via authenticated transport/released handler. Stale/malformed cannot broaden to management; plugin-origin direct calls denied.

Host enforces read/write ceilings/read-only effects before process operations. SQLite authorizes compiled SQL,excludes host paths,bounds values/complexity/concurrency. Product maps sessions/process adapters only; no new manifest/data flags.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Package sources and lifecycle
Production obtains catalog entries from the validated latest-only market snapshot. Publisher, plugin, version, hashes, signatures, revocation evidence, source policy, and Host requirements must match before ReDevPlugin changes the registry.

A GitHub source without an administrator-entered tag resolves the latest eligible Release on each new inspection; the previously resolved release tag is evidence, not a new durable user pin.

## Retained plugin data

ReDevPlugin 3.9 owns target-filtered discovery, exact inspection, one-shot recovery commit and read-only reconciliation. The source is an uninstalled instance with compatible retained data; the target must be explicitly disabled. The Host verifies owner, publisher, plugin identity, data shape, generation, management revision and active fingerprint. Its atomic transaction swaps data references while retaining both generations. It does not restore grants, secrets or enabled state.

Redeven passes published SDK DTOs unchanged. Discovery, inspection and status require environment read permission; commit requires write permission; disabling remains an admin action. An uncertain commit is never replayed. Reconciliation uses the exact inspected plan; a confirmed pending result permits a new explicit review, while unknown status remains read-only. Host restart recovery remains upstream-owned.

## Plugin data upgrades

ReDevPlugin 3.10 owns package-declared conversion, isolated input/output generations, quotas, cancellation, and the atomic package/data/history transaction. A converter matches an exact predecessor version and data shape. Failed or cancelled conversion keeps the old package and data; committed or unknown outcomes use the existing update reconciliation path and never trigger automatic replay. Downgrade restores the exact historical package's last data generation. The platform migrates its control store before opening it; Redeven never reads or writes that schema.

Redeven consumes the verified data-upgrade declaration from the released security summary. Review presents one concise saved-data notice before approval; method, predecessor identities and resource limits remain in expandable package details. Added, changed and removed declarations use the existing security-difference projection. Review omits empty release-note placeholders and generic instructions; inspection-binding facts stay inside expandable evidence, and unchanged permission grants appear only once. No second migration wizard, converter dispatcher, durable job or product-owned data copy is introduced.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Host modules and external packages
Redeven constructs the released Host with explicit core, official-release, runtime, connectivity, secrets, capability, and external-package modules. Redeven supplies session, authorization, web-security, trust, official release-source, observability, secret, external source, and business adapters; it never edits registry, inspection, token, lease, revoke-epoch, or plugin-data state directly.

The official signed-release module remains the stricter release-ref path.

## Network adapter

The product-owned hostnetwork package implements current host routing without
network I/O in its constructor. HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY use explicit
upper/lowercase environment settings, including explicit empty values for direct
routing; NO_PROXY is evaluated with the standard hostname/IP/CIDR matcher. On
macOS, requests without applicable environment policy use CFNetwork system
settings and bounded cancellable PAC resolution. Linux uses environment proxies
or normal OS routing. Remote Runtimes use their own host network environment.

The adapter respects the ordered configured routes. A bodyless GET/HEAD may try
the next configured route only after a dial failure before an application
connection exists. It never invents a direct fallback. TLS, protocol and unknown
outcome errors do not change routes. Writes use fresh HTTP/1 connections and are
not automatically replayed, including when the application supplies an idempotency
header. Read and write requests share a bounded eight-request limit per transport;
read pools retain at most two idle connections per origin for thirty seconds.

Market services own their default transport. The plugin integration closes its
caller-owned package transport on failure or shutdown. Each granted connector
receives an independent transport managed by the upstream pool lifecycle. TLS
verification and system trust roots remain enabled; proxy credentials stay on the
proxy hop and never become origin or plugin credentials.

## Reviewed connections

Connection inventory requires effective read access. Review, approval, cancellation
and revocation require an authenticated administrator with effective read, write
and execute access. The private-network adapter checks the exact cached session
and explicit nonempty prefixes using the published destination classifier;
metadata endpoints, unspecified addresses and blanket prefixes stay denied.
Upstream owns exact destination binding, address pinning, revisions, expiry,
leases and revocation. Installing a package grants no connection authority.

Plugin Center presents verified installed connector declarations, a separate
review and approval, exact destination/methods/private prefixes/secret reference,
and both connection and review expiry. Owner, active package, revision or policy
changes retire pending UI state. An uncertain approval is never replayed; the
client lists current authority before enabling another write. Failed reconciliation
keeps mutations disabled until an explicit successful refresh.

The connectivity executor retains the released 1 MiB request/response defaults.
Large application transfers require explicitly designed bounded requests; the
qualification fixture transfers 64 MiB as 64 one-MiB requests per direction and
also requires oversized requests and responses to fail. It does not certify a
single 64 MiB HTTP request or relax platform quotas.

## Surfaces and interaction ownership
The product Shell owns one released `PluginPlatformClient`, authenticated transport, and shared surface scope.

The application-method receiver (`surface.methods`) uses the same read authorization as opening and preparing its surface. The receiver registers, polls, and responds only within the platform-validated surface, gateway token, bridge channel, and frame generation. Registering a receiver grants no document write access: each intent invocation still passes its declared method effect, local policy, schema, and confirmation checks.

Redeven uses them for host placement behavior, never as identity, authorization, or permission evidence.

A recovery presentation may explain or retry the Host snapshot, but it is not a second open gate and owns no catch-up identity state machine.

## Web origin adapter

Redeven derives a plugin origin only from a trusted product entry origin and the released surface origin key. Local UI and AppServer route child requests to the released Web surface handler after removing parent credentials. Desktop, Gateway and Center own the product transport and origin routing; package assets, tickets and surface bridge semantics remain upstream-owned.

Ordinary HTTP loopback Local UI uses the same isolated resource handler as
Desktop. Its child authority must derive from a current public loopback parent
on the exact listener port. This is a resource route, not an additional public
management authority or a private-bridge fallback.

sections.body:
## Inventory and permissions
One authenticated fetch adapter/client/scope/placement coordinator serves Env App. Mutations carry current management and applicable policy/revoke revisions. Committed/unknown outcomes use Host revocation then SDK scope teardown and refresh, never a second slot-close path or blind retry. Confirmation names exact permission IDs, not official-plugin labels.

## External changes
The first terminal error per surface refreshes owner-scoped inventory once, without execution replay or same-revision auto-retry. User Retry retires its failed slot, awaits authoritative inventory and opens only while original component/owner remain current. Failed reads never authorize cached-revision reopening.

The keyed lease replaces changed management revisions/generations; retired components cannot reopen duplicate slots. Enable first refreshes the instance, mutating its current revision only if still disabled. If already enabled elsewhere, refresh restores the container without another mutation.

Activity/Workbench share refresh with Plugin Center and placement. Refresh preserves layout, Agent/file effects and sibling surfaces. Failed reads retain healthy cached leases, not prove revocation; failed surfaces still need successful reads before retry. Refresh reads the latest owner-bound snapshot without suspending/detaching Workbench DOM: iframe detachment would reload consumed tickets and lose sibling state.

Synchronous visibility/theme/context delivery faults during retirement/navigation enter the same exact-slot first-error refresh/SDK retirement path. Never escape into Workbench's error boundary or close siblings.

## Installation recovery
Host startup observations bind instance ID, active fingerprint, installation timestamp and management revision. SDK compares current enabled inventory; both official/external projections preserve these fields and show only matches. Update/reinstall/disable/uninstall invalidates old observations without inferred readiness or another recovery pass; current sibling failures remain visible.

Explicit retry loading/results/rejections bind captured installation/authenticated session. Late replies cannot replace new installation state. Localize released reason codes; catalog instance IDs/raw unknown codes are not failure copy. Inventory action_state alone authorizes launch.

## Worker execution failures
Ordinary Worker budget, memory or deadline failures return to the application through released typed execution errors. They do not invalidate Surface authority, discard drafts or trigger replay. Authors own call-error presentation; host recovery handles terminal Surface failures only.

## Close and revocation
On narrow Plugin Center uninstall, return focus after modal exit to surviving detail heading, not hidden card. User close uses released request-close; unsaved work gets one localized Floe confirmation, preserving slot on cancel. Forced invalidation bypasses consent. Record successful request-close to prevent duplicate close on disposal.

SDK teardown may leave product layout while setting the document to about:blank, removing same-origin authority and closing bridge. Retained iframe geometry proves no application authority; reopening requires a fresh authorized slot.

macOS uses the exact remote Swift package in the existing Runtime helper.

The canonical official Alpine source remains the final fallback; every download still checks the expected size and SHA-256 before atomic cache publication, and a failed archive download can move to the next trusted source.

Capability normalization also applies to a retried connection after accepting or declining takeover, so a removed display cannot return through the stored request.

Control and media travel through separate Flowersec native proxy streams bound to the same product attachment. Cancellation retires the selection and releases held keys; lock-screen input cannot use that text path.

Native session and frame authority remain governed by this concept.

Compatibility epoch 35 requires both Desktop and Runtime to understand explicit reasoning `on` alongside the existing default, off, effort, and budget choices. Earlier clients reject `on`; ordinary epoch admission prevents a mixed pair from accepting a Flower or Desktop model-source request it cannot interpret. See the [reasoning selection contract](../ui/flower-reasoning-selection.md) for model capability and control semantics.

Epoch 59 pairs Runtime authorization requests with the shared Desktop and Env App OpenAI account picker. A saved registry requires an account selection or explicit new-registration intent; old Desktop clients must update before Flower access. Registration semantics belong to the [ChatGPT account lifecycle](../ai/chatgpt-account-lifecycle.md).

Epoch 65 requires the model directory's backend-owned default_fetch_source field in provider search policies. See [model web search](../ai/model-web-search.md).

Epoch 67 requires complete changed pin metadata in Flower pin confirmations. New pins append to the endpoint's existing order; Desktop and Runtime must agree on the changed ranks and revisions before a confirmation is accepted. See [sidebar pin ordering](../ui/flower-thread-sidebar.md).

Epoch 71 requires truthful per-attachment Gateway connection phases and a collection-only owner status API. Durable joining/joined/removal state is separate from live controller observations. A stopped Runtime cannot report a connected attachment. The shared projection, strict Desktop admission and independent Gateway epoch are defined by [Gateway interactions](../gateway/gateway-desktop-interactions.md).

Env App hydrates one terminal session catalog after protocol connection, environment readiness, and process permission. The catalog owns canonical session metadata, notification convergence, connection epoch, permission clearing, stale-on-disconnect state, and bounded early latest values.

Runtime persists `terminal_history_retention` with nullable `max_lines`/`max_bytes` safe nonnegative integers and applies those defaults before terminal readiness. Published terminal-go owns validation, native limit application, pruning, snapshot invalidation and atomic Presentation. Defaults affect only subsequently created sessions; existing sessions are never silently reconfigured.

`/_redeven_proxy/api/terminal/history-retention` is the product settings adapter: GET reads defaults or an authorized session; admin-only PUT persists and activates defaults; POST applies explicit limits to a session using its connection ID and transport generation. Session application reuses shell/container permission and ownership checks, is principal-bound, does not transfer controller ownership, and rejects stale attachments. Limits preserve process, live screen, geometry and content epoch, while invalidating historical snapshots through the upstream history epoch. No local implementation of terminal retention or RPC retry is introduced.

## AI Flower RPC registration
The local direct and remote agent production session profiles register the complete AI inventory before Flowersec freezes a session. A declared method therefore cannot fail at the router with a missing-handler 404. Stop remains one RPC lifecycle command without a fallback transport.

## Independent Gateway composition

The upstream-first review uses published Flowersec 5.11.1 WebSocketHTTPServerOptions.ApplicationHandler to compose client HTTP with Runtime transport on one TLS endpoint, and its egress.HTTPSProxy for explicit Runtime Cloud routing. No upstream mechanism change, local dependency overlay or copied implementation is required.

## Mechanism
The released runtime dependency set includes Floeterm terminal-go v0.20.0 and Flowersec Go v5.11.1.

Env App and Desktop consume Flowersec TypeScript v5.11.1.

Switching a Flower thread, Activity or Workbench mode, terminal view, or file consumer cannot reconnect Flowersec.

Terminal ownership, live framing, history, attachment arbitration, and warmup are specified in [Runtime terminal lifecycle](runtime-terminal-lifecycle.md); this concept only defines the Flowersec/Floeterm dependency boundary and shared transport admission.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Facts and actions
`ServiceFacts` separates presence, ownership, runtime state, inspection completeness, resource references, and check time.

Frontend code never substitutes Retry or Restart for unavailable Start.

A failed Host maintenance hook may be bypassed only through an administrator's reviewed plan, and only for verified resources.

## Review and execution
`GET /managed-web-services/{id}/inspection` requires read permission, is non-cacheable, and uses the same factual backend projection as the list.

Existing unrelated lifecycle transactions cannot be overwritten by recovery.

Instance-scoped allocation and legacy resource boundaries are owned by [Service resource ownership](service-resource-ownership.md).

## Uninstall transaction
Uninstall uses `runtime_manifest_json`, the existing operation coordinator, and the existing event stream.

A resource recreated under the same name cannot acquire the previous deletion authorization.

Detachment remains available while it is unresolved.

## Management archives and access
Registry version 4 adds `active`, `detached`, and `uninstalled`. Only active records participate in template uniqueness and must own an authorized Forward.

Names, ports, or cached reachability never prove ownership.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Shared behavior and host ownership
Shared desktop/src/envcenter owns routes/search/filter/recovery/order/cancellation/Gateway lists. Desktop adapter calls existing lifecycle/windows; Web calls Center HTTP/browser tabs. Shared code imports neither Electron/Node filesystem nor Web auth. Desktop never contacts Center or changes Welcome/navigation/preparation/shutdown. Config/secrets do not sync. cmd/center-contracts generates exact DTO/TS/schema bounds.

Labels/hostnames grant no trust. Revisions/sequences fence observations; late completion cannot navigate canceled pending tabs or cancel open route owners. Refresh reads authority, not new intent.

## Server entry
Portal, Env and each child use distinct HTTPS origins under one registrable domain/port with matching TLS. Bookmarks are direct. Clipboard denial/absence retains descriptor/manual localized selection; announce success only after actual write.

Center pairs as access-only Gateway after fingerprint confirmation. Runtime independently persists consent through redeven web-binding apply --stdin --yes, binding RuntimeID/origin/clientSPKI/scope/revision. Published Flowersec mutually authenticated TLS1.3 pins signed Runtime service; no inbound app TCP listener.

Operations bind device/route. Browser nonce/exact origins/bounded redemption/single-use code complete handoff; response-loss same-request retry recovers one outcome. Host-only cookies never replace Runtime password/MFA. Logout/security/source/route revocation cancels derived admissions/streams.

## Runtime and child applications
webbinding owns consent, webconnector pinned TLS, environmentcenter admin/directory/proxy. Deployment requires separate stateless Connector via Unix socket with exact peer UID before credentials. Worker holds admitted route credentials only; Center retains admin/factors/master key. Direct adapter is test-only, never deployment fallback.

Control connection owns worker lease; Center loss/logout/revocation closes all streams. Connector restart loses leases; next request requires fresh valid admission. Never replay business HTTP. Systemd/Compose use distinct unprivileged identities; Connector cannot read Center state/TLS keys. IPC preserves bounded permission/capacity/compatibility/offline codes; Runtime payloads cannot invent worker errors. Published controller retries only explicit transient Gateway admission conflicts; invalid/denied/revoked proofs terminate.

Services/editor/graphical viewers use resource origins; trusted proxy retains parent credentials. Editor pins running instance. Graphical access requires scoped Flowersec. Child framing follows authenticated Runtime policy for editor workers; Portal denies framing.

## Plugin application origins
Authenticated parent operations prepare/revoke origins under shared pending/active capacity. Duplicate pending origin is busy; failed/canceled probes release reservation. DELETE fences pending work so late probes cannot revive/replace generations. Each child binds parent route/Runtime admission and cannot call management APIs. Gateway certificates/CONNECT enforce exact namespace/target. Desktop credentials attach only to trusted parent frame.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Collection
Centered header/launcher/toolbar/list. Rows have 64px minimum, not fixed height. Bounded status isolates async feedback under [layout stability](../ui/asynchronous-layout-stability.md); narrow/localized text wraps.

## Opening restrictions
Unavailable Open retains its ordinary icon and native disabled state. Focusable wrapper exposes reason on keyboard/touch/hover; active work names action/stage. When backend offers executable Start, it is primary within existing permissions.

## Review and focus
One drawer shows conclusion, compact resources and recommended actions. New known inventory may replace old inspection; unknown preserves facts. Older/unknown targets retain stop-first then explicit update. Originally stopped services remain stopped after update.

## Templates and versions
Template categories use published Floe Tabs with paired selection colors, roving keyboard focus and a labelled panel. Product styles never override tab ink. Template lists use compact rounded rows with source groups; the wider detail pane keeps deployment facts, runtime details and actions together. Dropdown wrappers own the sole focus target and disabled state.

Both template and installed-service versions use the same bounded directory/detail workspace. Rows emphasize version and state; the selected detail owns trust, source, platform and expandable artifact identity. Current releases retain useful provenance. Narrow layouts stack independently scrollable panes, while request feedback and submission remain outside the list. Refresh and verification preserve selection, focus, scroll and footer geometry. Confirmation, stop-first and update authorization remain unchanged. Selection motion is brief and local; reduced motion removes travel.

## Execution feedback
Execution details keep one bounded command/output viewport. Downloaded bytes remain visible when the total is unknown; unknown totals keep the byte bar indeterminate. Speed is shown once measured bytes are available, while fully cached pulls show zero transfer. Layer counts remain separate. New output does not expand the panel or move a reader away from earlier lines.

sections.body:

Specific entrance errors remain readable; failed Open never prevents another attempt.

The shell retains only collection and loading-presentation styles; management and version-review styles load with the product page rather than the initial document graph.

scripts/dev_desktop.sh freezes HEAD/tracked/nonignored source; drift fails. Authored OKF/builders/Go embeds are inputs, generated OKF/ignored assets outputs. Keys bind normalized destination/port, authentication, SSH executable and credential scope. Preserve failure without substitution/replay. macOS/Linux use ControlMaster; Windows bounded native OpenSSH plus one child/private Bridge, never WSL/ControlMaster. Cancel only owned children.

Omitted passwords reuse exact private scope; explicit changes reject during leases and never cross scopes. Without password, explicit connections try configured keys/agent in batch mode even for password registrations; passive status may defer. Never send empty retries. Start/Restart/Update carry transient credentials through access/certificate checks, preparation and verification without saving; observations reject passwords.

Connect Timeout bounds probe/inventory/readiness; startup/packages have distinct deadlines. Windows x64 askpass accepts password/passphrase, rejects host-key prompts, writes only private stdout and preserves OpenSSH trust. Missing helper fails; no secrets in args/files/logs. Bounded includes exclude wildcard/negated picker aliases, not explicit destinations. Save exact root/container engine+ID separately from label.

## Execution
One operation reuses transport and probes platform once. Only inventory/stop prepares the small helper; Start/Stop never build full bundles. Update verifies before mutation with visible acquisition/upload/build. Use public dependencies and install Desktop deps before Env assets.

Archive bounds: 256 MiB compressed/512 MiB expanded including Runtime/Computer/signed plugins, enforced before writes and parsed once. Upload progress has its own stall deadline; command timeout resumes after final write. Stall/cancel/loss stops owned command; pipe bytes prove no receipt. Password prompts have no upload deadline.

Private slots: runtime/managed/bin/executables 0700, stamps/evidence 0600 independent of umask. Failed normalization preserves live slot; upstream owns executable admission. Host targets require confirmed user/root, containers exact saved identity. Start/Restart/Update/Reinstall may start container; Stop never does and accepts empty inventory. Signal only verified scope; retain before/after. Wipe-reinstall may tolerate helper inventory/stop failure only when direct access can isolate root.

Remote snippets perform bounded probe/stage/inventory/stop/install/start/verify/isolate/cleanup. Desktop owns order/deadlines/cancel/progress/retry; no target lock/heartbeat/supervisor.

## Progress and results
Use generated signed GitHub latest/download/redeven-install.sh with selected tag, no Portal duplicate. One Launcher Operation measures actual upload/download/acquisition bytes. Parse complete Downloading Redeven: N% records; stderr diagnostics, stdout stage path. Companion output cannot reset Runtime progress. No additional parser/process/poll.

100% transfer proves no activation/readiness. Freeze measured progress on failure/cancel. Acquisition/staging/upload/unpack are preparation; only activation changes live slot. Create operation before first SSH command. Distinguish connection/engine/preparation/command/readiness errors with technical stderr. Empty successful report stays pending to deadline; nonzero read is command failure, valid blocked report Runtime failure, only nonempty malformed report invalid. All lifecycle paths share interpretation.

## Recovery presentation
Recovery uses an unboxed layout within the existing shell, with generous whitespace, semantic theme colors, standard buttons, and fine separators around the authoritative countdown or active phase.

A 30-second stalled-app timeout shows an actionable failure instead of an endless loading surface.

## Mechanism
Each established bridge owns one immutable transport-recovery snapshot with a monotonic `generation` and `revision`, the real `waiting`, `connecting`, `paused`, `ready`, or `failed` phase, completed attempt count, known retry and recovery timestamps, a structured failure, and explicitly allowed actions.

Lifecycle generation fencing cancels matching Opens so a late response cannot recreate the old session.

## Discovery and registration
The main process publishes one immutable platform-capability snapshot. Renderer surfaces consume it and never infer the host operating system.

UI recovery copy may show Microsoft WSL commands for the user to run.

## Linux Runtime lifecycle
WSL and SSH host operations consume the same managed-Linux probe, uploaded install, atomic activation, startup report, inventory, exact stop, and verification scripts.

Runtime installs under the Linux user's home-backed `~/.redeven`, never under `/mnt`, and does not require `systemd`.

Only the Environment Stop action stops it.

## Private Bridge and failure behavior
`desktop-bridge` remains a foreground `wsl.exe` child carrying the shared `redeven-desktop-placement-h2/1` HTTP/2 session over private standard input and output.

Multiple registered distributions have independent target ids, processes, Bridges, update state, and lifecycle coordinator keys.

## Package and update boundary
The Windows Desktop bundle uses `managed_wsl_archive` and contains one verified `redeven_linux_amd64.tar.gz`; it must not contain or execute `redeven.exe`.

Public Windows assets remain forbidden until Authenticode signing, signed NSIS update metadata, signing receipts, and a real signed n-1 to n update are enabled together.

Desktop delegates to its bundled Runtime's `host-application-package` command. Different architectures can reuse identical common files; all others must match their pinned catalog entry.

Other component consumers do not inherit this product's eviction policy.

The initiating Desktop document owns its subprocess and temporary ZIP.

The [preparation contract](../architecture/host-application-preparation.md) owns those boundaries and pending application opening.

## Honest progress and recovery
The delivery choice explains that Desktop reuses its cache and downloads only missing components.

After explicit preparation, waiting and checking have unknown cache/download totals and no percentage.

Closing a reserved app window still retires its launch intention.

## Layout
The first-party host-application bootstrap places its controls in one 40-pixel Desktop titlebar, alongside platform-owned traffic lights or caption buttons. Empty header space drags the window when no toolbar popover is open; buttons and popovers explicitly reject dragging.

The control is unavailable until its selected target has decoded pixels.

## Appearance and language
The bootstrap consumes published Floe `standalone.css`: primitive sizing and fonts, all 26 shell presets, shared floating material and input focus rules. Local CSS owns only viewer layout and maps control states to upstream semantic tokens; it must not maintain a second light/dark palette.

The inline assets add no request or connection wait.

## Backend commands
The shared toolbar and picture-preset presentation do not own backend state. macOS retains native menu, window-generation, frame credit and capture-quality semantics.

It never sends server shutdown or force-kills the application. macOS quit retains its existing application-wide confirmation. These distinct actions must not be collapsed into one destructive command.

replaces only a marked main-document response with a localized, scriptless
explanation using published Floe window-status assets. The initial view shows a
short title without a primary action. A native, initially collapsed View details disclosure
reveals the reason, original service address with its current path, query and
fragment, and Copy address. It does not suggest retries or direct access. The toolbar
remains the sole address editor. Copy uses the host-projected address and acknowledges
completion in place. Only the exact current host document can request this action.

to another address restores ordinary browsing. System-browser opening is disabled

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reverse application streams
After local consent, Runtime redeems its invitation with its own identity and initiates a persistent Flowersec session to the unified public TLS endpoint. Gateway opens a reverse ByteStream on that Runtime's connection and relays both streams with bounded buffers and cancellation.

TLS, WebSocket, streaming responses and secure cookies retain their original semantics.

## Application and management separation
A reverse stream enters the original public Runtime handler. It never acquires a trusted Desktop management marker.

The catalog alone does not authorize service or Runtime process operations.

## Limits and revocation
The shared budget admits at most 32 business connections per member and 1,024 in total, including pending opens. One member exceeding a limit cannot consume another member's allocation.

Revoking a client closes its live streams and fences its pending artifacts. Other clients and the Runtime attachment stay connected. Reauthorization uses a fresh key, so previous artifacts never regain admission. These effects use published Flowersec session cancellation and relay primitives.

Cloud authorization never closes independent Gateway streams. Local egress cancellation is scoped separately by [Optional Runtime Cloud egress](gateway-cloud-access.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Invitations
Host-issued Runtime invitations require Runtime authentication and explicit consent. Client packages are rdgc1/purpose redeven-gateway-client/version1: one-use secret, exact Gateway ID/key, scoped CA and expiry. Parsers reject cross-purpose use, unknown fields, malformed trust and expiry.

Verify HTTPS using only that CA, then signed Gateway identity before persisting device trust. Never disable TLS or install global CAs. Packages expire after ten minutes; consumption admits no second device. Identical original completion may recover response loss. Desktop/Center retain CA in independent records; display names authenticate nothing. Revocation closes that device's channels without affecting another client/Cloud user.

## Private management
Local/SSH/container adapters verify credentials over the private host socket; public URLs expose device access only. Gateway derives capabilities, never caller-selected/persisted device roles. manage_attachments covers invitations/removal; manage_network covers endpoints/listeners/Host restrictions/egress/reevaluation. Issuance/listing/revocation/receipts require current host proof. Both management capabilities exist together only on that verified request. Removing a Desktop registration preserves remote service/data.

All public device keys are listed/revocable, including host-paired keys. Historical host_managed grants no exemption. Trust schema4 atomically migrates1–3 before readiness, preserving identity/access/revocations; unsupported state stays unchanged.

Private management uses host proof independently of device signatures, but a supplied signature must verify. Signed identity retains requested binding audience for exact connection pinning. Applications/service identity require admitted device keys even over private socket. Self-revocation preserves private management/recovery; refresh cannot pair again. Explicit reauthorization creates a fresh key; challenges/old receipts cannot revive revoked keys.

## Mutation recovery
X-Redeven-Operation-ID binds private mutations. A bounded mode-0600 host-only journal persists intent before effect, response afterward. Same ID/body returns saved result; route/body changes conflict. POST /gateway/v6/operations/query reads the original over the private channel. Retain <=1024 operations/24h. Issuance receipts may contain short-lived packages; never expose journal data in diagnostics/public replies. Expiry grants no replay.

Interrupted effect-before-receipt yields OPERATION_RESULT_UNKNOWN without replay. Desktop stores ID privately and queries after response loss. Confirmed failure clears pending state; unknown/expired stays fenced with inspectable ID. Explicit review acknowledgement clears only the verified Gateway's recovery fence. CLI supports --operation-id and operations query --operation-id, exposing ID on failure. Join/rotation/Cloud route/enrollment keep their domain receipts; refresh cannot authorize/resubmit consent.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Independent enrollment
Runtime owns one Cloud association, owner-issued setup authorization and its existing Flowersec connection controller. Gateway attachment consent cannot authorize Cloud registration. Attachment lookup uses an explicit Gateway identity, or the sole attachment when unambiguous; a selected Cloud route never supplies a default attachment for general lookup or removal. Runtime may select a Gateway route before initial Cloud enrollment, using route/association revision zero; enrollment verifies the actual Cloud target when it becomes known.

Route operations retain an operation ID, expected revisions, target fingerprint, confirmation and queryable result. Changing an attachment, certificate, route or Cloud identity invalidates previous consent. An unknown result queries the original operation. A canceled committed operation remains committed.

## Local egress
New Gateways deny egress with an empty destination list. Host administrators configure exact canonical host:port destinations and per-attachment inherit/allow/deny overrides. Wildcards, URLs, paths, duplicate or malformed authorities are rejected. Executable policy uses attachment.admit, access.open and egress.open; no Cloud approval is consulted.

Admission requires the current Runtime attachment certificate, current local policy and unexpired credentials. The published Flowersec HTTPSProxy carries inner HTTPS without exporting Runtime Cloud keys. Public product policy rejects private resolved destinations; the isolated acceptance harness explicitly opts into its private fixture network. No unrestricted proxy or global proxy environment mutation is introduced.

Disabled egress closes only egress reservations. Independent reverse application streams remain available. Removing an attachment closes all streams depending on that attachment. Credential expiry and stale timers cannot restore withdrawn policy. Policy snapshots copy destination lists so callers cannot widen authority by mutating them.

The catalog's effective_egress_allowed is a policy decision, not a reachability result. It combines the active attachment, inherit/allow/deny and the hook decision for the current policy revision. Egress admission requires an active eligible attachment, its current unexpired client certificate and an allowed destination. The authenticated CONNECT request is independent of the reverse application connection: a disconnected reverse channel does not withdraw egress authority, while attachment removal, certificate replacement and policy revocation do. Only a completed route preflight proves the tested destination was reachable at that time. Empty destinations disable forwarding even when policy permission is true.

Reevaluate egress policy uses manage_network, applies only the selected attachment version and committed policy, and runs no application-health or Cloud-registration test. Unsaved editor changes remain drafts. Access.open hooks continue to evaluate individual sessions; this action does not reevaluate that domain.

## No fallback or cross-path revocation
Runtime registration, recovery, Cloud transport and enabled official-platform traffic use the explicitly chosen route. Route failure reports unavailable; it never silently dials Cloud directly. Cloud logout, user removal or binding revocation cannot alter Gateway device trust, attachments or environment passwords/MFA. Cloud sessions remain subject to their own authorization and Runtime security checks.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity
`connection_id/connectionID` identifies saved registrations across IPC, progress, sessions and Center; Web Center maps `source_id` to it. `gateway_id/gatewayID` identifies signed trust/attachments. DesktopGatewayAttachment and Center environments are projections; DesktopRuntimeTargetID/placement owns lifecycle. Addresses/Cloud routes replace neither ID. Reject ambiguous/retired IPC fields; update main/renderer together, preserving stored IDs, credentials, keys and schema5.

One runtime_connection_target projects management/derived Cloud facts. Gateway access is independent of Cloud association/capability/route; Cloud mutations and attachment errors retain separate coordination/domains.

## Enrollment session
Use a padded, content-sized selector with Dropdown and trailing Cancel; empty inventory offers recovery. Selection opens the fixed-height wizard; wrapped/touch content retains natural height.

Creation offers Not now/Add Gateway access. Each opening leases the exact sender/target bridge and connects before fresh verification/consent. Env App close retains the lease; cancel, navigation, destruction or authority change retires it. Admitted writes retain transport until settlement; reject late submissions.

Try saved management/SSH/OpenSSH credentials first. Passive auth_required/missing credentials cannot preempt; only typed current auth failure reveals focused temporary credentials with Enter and stops credential-free retries. Separate auth/Gateway/engine faults; unknown is not denial. Never save passwords or infer consent. Retain credentials through admitted action/access verification, clearing on completion/failure/close without observation races.

Confirmed stopped offers Start. Start/restart/update/reinstall share lifecycle owner; ask SSH credentials only after typed failure. Loss stops submissions/polls, preserving drafts. Explicit recovery, authority change or Settings suspension revokes verification/consent; resume with fresh lease/connection and step/code drafts. Observation cannot cancel admitted work.

## Invitation and completion
Saved/manual tabs retain independent drafts/nodes. Select enabled registration IDs. Endpoint-less registrations retain guidance; use confirmed endpoints or canonical HTTPS origin, never SSH/listener coordinates. Reject changed trust, Host-rejected origin or remote loopback without hiding registrations. Inventory preserves typing; removed usable addresses revoke verification.

Shared-address editing needs manage_network/update_gateway_endpoints, without listener/restriction changes. IPC address persists only until catalog change. Admission needs explicit invite_gateway_runtime or pasted code plus Runtime verification/consent; save/select/issue alone is insufficient. Access-only shows administrator guidance. Close/suspend/authority change fences replies; success consumes code; reopen clears code/consent.

Owner API always returns attachments/counts/runtime_running/observed_at_unix_ms. attachment_state is durable; connection_state observed; phase is presentation. Connected requires current controller. Unknown/connecting/disconnected/failed/stopped differ. CLI/running Runtime share projection; counts prove no connectivity. Epoch71 rejects legacy aggregates/contradictions.

Success requires exact admitted non-removing attachment; absent/unrelated results stay uncertain. Unknown submissions query exact membership without replay: positive completes, authoritative absence clears uncertain/consumed material and returns verification. Checks consume no code; Done restores origin focus. No Cloud choice/existing-environment DTO. Replacement requires sole attachment; otherwise add/verify new Gateway, explicitly change Cloud route if needed, remove old.

## Welcome/management
Retain toolbar, horizontal Environment/Redeven Cloud/Gateway navigation and bottom bar. Details hide search/filter/description; localized All Gateways restores search/scroll/focus. Narrow cards use one column. Name/Manage opens the five sections in-shell; global navigation suspends owners, preserving drafts.

Cards group identity/management, equal full-row Connect client/Runtime and fixed-height status/refresh. Catalog failure outranks readiness. Anchored help avoids reflow; trust stays in details. Use Floe Manage/More geometry/touch; access-only omits enrollment. Edit/Enable/Disable/confirmed Remove disclose retained service/membership. Initialize trust/local policy separately; URLs grant no administration. Filtering preserves action owners without hidden maintenance cards.

Creation separates service/deployment from URL pairing/host transport. Save opens exact registration status/action without proving connectivity/deployment. Include stopped/unopened managed Runtimes; other-admin uses the existing issuer; missing addresses link Network. Await modal exit. Hide retains drafts/work; reopen renews management/consent via card actions without duplicate issuers/banners.

Use a bounded reading column and icon navigation/toolbar; selection uses fill/weight. Overview prioritizes address/actions and collapses identity. Clients shows counts/illustrated emptiness; narrow identity/time/actions stack. Network aligns labels/values and maintenance edges, with ordinary path/listener fonts and on-demand help. Times retain exact localized tooltips. Match input/action heights/touch targets. Resize help next frame; cancel on disposal. One availability owner clears recovered feedback while retaining drafts/invalidated credentials. Visited panels stay mounted; only active sections affect scroll extent. Below768px, scroll full navigation labels. Dialogs restore focus; empty cards show counts. Use semantic tokens and every explicit locale. Build inequality cannot invent actions or reinterpret rejection; reuse compatible [services](gateway-service.md).

Runtimes owns attachments/egress overrides/reevaluate/remove; Network owns destinations/default egress; Clients owns listing/revoke/current-device/fresh-key reauthorization. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Authority ownership
Gateway owns its stable identity, paired client keys, Runtime attachments, local network policy and active transports. Runtime explicitly consents to each attachment and owns its application TLS identity, environment password/MFA, sessions and host execution restrictions. Gateway administration grants no Runtime lifecycle or application authority. Desktop and Web Center provide the environment directory and opening experience; Gateway catalogs only describe attached Runtimes. The authorized platform model gateway is a separate Cloud AI endpoint, not this service. Device access, host administration and Runtime application authorization are independently verified. Desktop and Web Center hold their own client identities; saved host coordinates and client observations confer no management authority.

Gateway has no Cloud machine registration, Namespace assignment, management renewal, delegated Runtime publication or Cloud command receiver. Runtime may independently enroll with Cloud. Gateway failure affects only traffic using that Gateway.

## Public and private endpoints
One advertised HTTPS origin serves client pairing/identity/catalog/application admission, Runtime invitation exchange/enrollment/mTLS attachment, and optional restricted egress. All advertised origins prove one stable Gateway identity. Host restrictions apply before protocol admission. The public handler never mounts management or operation-query routes.

The native Gateway packages support Linux and macOS. Administration uses a temporary private directory (0700), Unix socket (0600), and private host credential. SSH/container bridges reach that same host socket. A loopback TCP address or request header is not host proof. Windows Desktop manages remote/container Gateways; this change does not introduce a native Windows Gateway package or named-pipe implementation.

## State and lifecycle
Gateway state schema 6 owns local attachments and policy; authority epoch 70 owns the independent Gateway wire break. Unsupported attachment state and retired cloud-access.json fail before creating identities or rewriting data. Desktop saved-connection schema 5 migrates its local locator to connection_id while retaining the independently pinned gateway_id and device credentials.

Trust schema 4 removes historical host classification while preserving every device identity and revocation. Attachment schema 6 and saved-connection schema 5 do not change. Runtime epoch 71 owns its new observation response; it does not advance Gateway epoch 70.

Explicit host maintenance is independent of client-device admission and prior service observations. Update and ordinary reinstall replace only the managed package, preserving configuration, identity and client access. Unsupported state still fails unchanged; reinstall is never an implicit schema migration.

Host-only configuration-reset requires an explicit existing state root, --confirm, a stopped service and valid existing private trust file. It archives Gateway-owned attachment, network/policy-hook, retired Cloud and host-operation configuration under a private configuration-history/reset-* directory, retaining device identity and revocations. Unsafe paths fail before moving files. A durable reset marker fences startup and repeat reset during interrupted file moves. Ordinary move failures roll back; uncertain failures retain the marker/archive for host inspection, never automatic replay. Reset requires reconnecting Runtimes and configuring network policy. Desktop exposes it as a separately confirmed reinstall option, prepares and verifies the package before reset, then starts and reconnects through host management. No public endpoint can invoke it.

Saving, refresh, pairing and attachment management never implicitly start a stopped service. Removing a Desktop connection does not remove remote attachments or stop its service. Release/build metadata is diagnostic; unrelated Runtime releases do not change Gateway authority.

Fast checks cover indexed records, queues, windows, turn/disclosure identity, block invalidation, keyed disposal, local thinking, structural/mutable dependencies, sealed bodies and incremental Markdown. Each sequence entry has one mounted owner; classification stays stable while live fields and first-prose boundaries update. Removed owners dispose. sections.title: Contract

Qualify these independent boundaries with native/viewer/API fixtures:

- Reuse an existing single-instance Mac process and preserve it after lease release. A 48-second first-window fixture must wait without relaunch.
- Multiwindow picker counts/literal titles preserve selection/focus; canceled close/quit retains process, pixels, sharing and explicit retry. Last lease release ends sharing, never the application.
- Unreadable/replaced surfaces never expire into closure. Confirmed final-window closure ends established physical viewers. Linux dialog-only apps reveal native-sized decoded dialogs.
- Stale quit selection rejects the whole set before termination. Unknown outcome retains error without inferred exit/retry. Read-only callers may list but cannot quit/detach.
- Network/reload retains process, suspends input/capture, frees buffers and reconnects the same session/current credential. Successor viewer revokes prior input/releases held keys/suspends capture first.
- Permission loss/lock has distinct recovery. Helper exit is sharing failure, not app exit; retire route/credential/buffers/helper before terminal state. Ignore late callbacks and retain unknown-terminal pages.
- Unproven foreground/window identity rejects input without replay/retargeting. Missing decoder negotiates same-process image transport.

Toolbar qualification: fixed bar with resizable content, bounded 320/390/1000 px popovers, keyboard menus, separate close/confirmed quit, late dismissal and no unconfirmed replay. Native quit covers catalog/session controls, visible/windowless apps, cancellation and stale generations.

## Reproducible measurements
Compare baseline and candidate on the same host, browser version, source size and workload.

An SSH tunnel changes transport overhead and must be recorded.

| Metric | Definition and controlled viewer acceptance budget |
| --- | --- |
| Input to presented pixels | DOM key event through remote application to changed canvas pixels on the next animation frame; nearest-rank P95 of 20 samples below 150 ms in every mode |
| Input during motion | The same 20-sample measurement while document scroll continues; P95 below 250 ms, including Save data cadence |
| Presented FPS | At most one changed-canvas presentation per animation frame; Motion first at least 25 FPS during document scroll |
| Received payload | All incoming WebSocket data bytes, including JSON; excludes WebSocket/TLS/SSH framing and network retransmissions |
| Idle bandwidth | Below 0.25 Mb/s after settling; a fully unchanged document should send zero image bytes |
| Document-motion bandwidth | Below 5 Mb/s for Automatic/Clarity/Save data and 15 Mb/s for Motion first at the recorded source size |
| Decode work | No more than two current-target frames plus one retired decode; no reconnect on a picture change |
| First frame | Navigation to first decoded canvas presentation; excludes browser-process launch before the viewer attaches |

concepts.summary:
ReDevPlugin 3.15.0 improves measured warm execution and Redeven restores only
initially visible plugin placements. Opened surfaces retain their independent
slots, drafts, selection and pending work when hidden. This is conditional lazy

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Consume the coordinated published Go/npm/Rust release, without local overrides.
Rust 1.98.0 builds the Wasmtime 50 runtime. The macOS helper keeps hardened
runtime with exactly the executable-memory exception required by upstream;
staging, cache identity and consumption verify the actual signed entitlement.
The executable is product-built; source-package provenance is not product
signing evidence. Release signing still requires the product identity.

Each first open captures current context/revision. Unopened close succeeds and
prevents later opening. Visibility never cancels an already started invocation,
replays an uncertain write or reuses revoked authority. Ordinary Worker errors
remain application-owned; they do not destroy a Surface. See
[recovery](../architecture/redevplugin-surface-recovery.md).

sections.title: Measurement
sections.body:
November 3, 2026, macOS/arm64, Node 26.7.0, Go 1.27.3 and Rust 1.98.0. Redeven
baseline is 2433435341c55aa34013de78c1ab023277d96639. Both UI variants use published
ReDevPlugin 3.15.0/Floe 0.87.2 and the same production Integration HTTP server,
including durable Host state. The old component alone is substituted in the
test build. Fifteen alternating fresh-browser pairs per scenario produce 60
trials; paired ratios use 10,000 deterministic bootstrap resamples.

| Scenario | Baseline median | Candidate median | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| One visible placement, active ready | 132.4 ms | 57.5 ms | Paired 2.315x, 95% interval 2.167–2.371 |
| One visible, incremental process-tree RSS | 867.59 MiB | 105.86 MiB | 87.8% less; ten frames versus one |
| First deferred activation | 0.1 ms | 49.1 ms | Candidate P95 53.99 ms; explicit first-use cost |
| Ten visible, all ready | 134.3 ms | 133.8 ms | No material regression; ten independent frames |
| Fresh Worker process/state, total | 335.68 ms | 504.05 ms | +168.37 ms; below predeclared 1 s echo budget |
| First Worker call | 6.05 ms | 4.39 ms | Excludes setup |
| 64 KV writes, individual versus batch | 225.5 ms | 4.55 ms | Paired 50.34x; exact values and rollback |
| Six schema statements, individual versus transaction | 48.15 ms | 8.15 ms | Paired 5.63x; trigger behavior retained |

Cold results use fifteen alternating pairs with identical historical 3.14 echo
guest bytes, fresh Integration/process/plugin state and warm OS file cache.
Candidate install/grant/prewarm is 186.86 ms versus 78.49 ms. Current 3.15 author
output also passes a separate live hardened-runtime smoke. These are not heavy
editor startup or network SLAs. Batch figures compare existing transports under
3.15, not a claim that every plugin becomes 50x faster. The six-statement case
does not measure complete Memos Worker bootstrap.

The product resource path preserves 1/32 MiB content; observed read chunks are
at most 2 MiB. Upload source Blobs are resident, so no bounded upload-memory
claim is made. Process-tree RSS includes shared pages and is not a leak proof.

Upstream paired production calls (ten rounds) reduce C4/C8 P95 from
7.721/15.530 ms to 4.165/7.662 ms; throughput increases from 765/735 to
1,751/1,662 requests/s. Mix/sort full-call paired speedups are 3.98x/8.49x.
Implementation attribution is b314dc13590bacb756579fc509334dd69ef1520b;
8b9b9fc12e273f86091a9d1029d7adb1ecdd43cf adds hardened-runtime qualification.
Both feature and main 13-stage gates, Quick CI and v3.15.0 public completion
